title.zh: 卷三百二十九 列傳第八十八 常秩 鄧綰 李定 舒亶 蹇周輔 徐鐸 王廣淵 王陶 王子韶 何正臣 陳繹
title.en: Volume 329 Biographies 88: Chang Zhi, Deng Wan, Li Ding, Shu Dan, Jian Zhoufu, Xu Duo, Wang Guangyuan, Wang Tao, Wang Zishao, He Zhengchen, Chen Yi
title.raw: 卷三百二十九 列傳第八十八 常秩 鄧綰 李定 舒亶 蹇周輔 徐鐸 王廣淵 王陶 王子韶 何正臣 陳繹 Volume 329 Biographies 88: Chang Zhi, Deng Wan, Li Ding, Shu Dan, Jian Zhoufu, Xu Duo, Wang Guangyuan, Wang Tao, Wang Zishao, He Zhengchen, Chen Yi

sentences.zh: 常秩，字夷甫，潁州汝陰人。

translations.literal: Chang Zhi, styled Yifu, was a native of Ruyin in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Zhi, who styled himself Yifu, came from Ruyin in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士不中，屏居里巷，以經術著稱。

translations.literal: He took the jinshi examination but failed, withdrew to live in his lane, and became renowned for classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the jinshi examination, secluded himself in his neighborhood, and won fame for his mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，賜束帛，為潁州教授，除國子直講，又以為大理評事。

translations.literal: During the Jiayou era he was granted silk, made professor at Ying Prefecture, appointed Direct Lecturer at the Directorate of Education, and also made Assessor at the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiayou period he received a gift of silk, served as professor in Ying Prefecture, was appointed Direct Lecturer at the Imperial University, and was also named Assessor at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 治平中，授忠武軍節度推官、知長葛縣，皆不受。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era he was offered the posts of military adjutant of the Zhongwu Army and magistrate of Changge County, but accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhiping period he was offered the posts of adjutant of the Zhongwu military commission and magistrate of Changge County, and declined them all.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，三使往聘，辭。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor ascended the throne, envoys were sent three times to invite him, but he declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenzong took the throne, the court sent envoys three times to summon him, and each time he refused.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，詔郡「以禮敦遣，毋聽秩辭」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining an edict ordered the prefecture to "send him off with ceremony and do not heed Zhi's refusals."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining, an edict told the prefecture to escort him to court with full ceremony and not to accept his excuses.

sentences.zh: 明年，始詣闕，帝曰：「先朝累命，何為不起？」

translations.literal: The next year he first came to the palace; the emperor said, "The previous reign summoned you repeatedly—why did you not rise?"
translations.idiomatic: The following year he finally appeared at court. The emperor asked, "The former emperor summoned you again and again—why did you stay away?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「先帝亮臣之愚，故得安閭巷。

translations.literal: He replied, "The former emperor understood my dullness, so I could dwell in peace in my lane.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The late emperor saw how limited I was, so I was allowed to live quietly in my neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 今陛下嚴詔趣迫，是以不敢不來，非有所決擇去就也。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's stern edict presses me urgently, so I dare not fail to come—not because I have chosen between going and staying."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's strict summons leaves me no choice, so I had to come—not because I weighed staying against serving."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，徐問之：「今何道免民於凍餒？」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and asked him gently, "What course now would save the people from cold and hunger?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and asked gently, "What policy would free the people from cold and hunger?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「法制不立，庶民食侯食，服侯服，此今日大患也。

translations.literal: He replied, "When institutions are not established, commoners eat the lord's food and wear the lord's clothes—this is today's great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Without sound institutions, ordinary people live on what lords provide and wear what lords supply—that is the great evil of our age.

sentences.zh: 臣才不適用，願得辭歸。」

translations.literal: My talent is not suited to use; I wish to be allowed to resign and return."
translations.idiomatic: My abilities are not fit for service; I ask permission to go home."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「既來，安得不少留？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Since you have come, how can you not stay a little?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Now that you are here, how can you leave at once?

sentences.zh: 異日不能用卿，乃當去耳。」

translations.literal: Only when one day I cannot use you should you go."
translations.idiomatic: When the day comes that I cannot employ you, then you may leave."

sentences.zh: 即拜右正言、直集賢院、管幹國子監，俄兼直舍人院，遷天章閣侍講、同修起居注，仍使供諫職，復乞歸，改判太常寺。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed Right Remonstrator, Direct Academician of the Jixian Hall, Administrator of the Directorate of Education, soon also Concurrent Custodian of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, promoted to Lecturer at the Hall of Heavenly Writings, Concurrent Compiler of the Imperial Diary, still charged with remonstrance duties; he again begged to return and was reassigned to judge the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately made Right Remonstrator, a direct academician of the Jixian Hall, and put in charge of the Imperial University; soon he also served in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, was promoted to lecturer at the Hall of Heavenly Writings and concurrent compiler of the imperial diary, and was still expected to remonstrate. He again asked to retire and was transferred to judge the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 七年，進寶文閣待制兼侍讀，命其子立校書崇文院。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was advanced to Academician Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Treasured Writings with the concurrent title Lecturer, and his son Li was ordered to proofread at the Hall of Cultivated Talents.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to awaiting-orders academician at the Hall of Treasured Writings and concurrent lecturer, and his son Li was appointed proofreader at the Hall of Cultivated Talents.

sentences.zh: 九年，病不能朝，提舉中太一宮、判西京留司御史臺，還潁。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, ill and unable to attend court, he was put in charge of the Central Great Unity Palace and made judge of the Western Capital Remonstrance Bureau, then returned to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, too ill to attend court, he was assigned to the Central Great Unity Palace and made judge of the Western Capital remonstrance bureau, then went home to Ying.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，年五十九，贈右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died at fifty-nine; he was posthumously given the title of Right Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died at fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Right Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 秩平居為學求自得。

translations.literal: In ordinary life Zhi pursued learning to gain understanding for himself.
translations.idiomatic: In private life Zhi studied to reach his own understanding.

sentences.zh: 王回，里中名士也，每見秩與語，輒欿然自以為不及。

translations.literal: Wang Hui, a celebrated man of the district, whenever he met Zhi and spoke with him would sigh that he himself could not measure up.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui, a noted local gentleman, would sigh after every conversation with Zhi that he himself fell short.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修、胡宿、呂公著、王陶、沈遘、王安石皆稱薦之。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu, Hu Su, Lü Gongzhu, Wang Tao, Shen Kui, and Wang Anshi all praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu, Hu Su, Lü Gongzhu, Wang Tao, Shen Kui, and Wang Anshi all praised and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 翕然名重一時。

translations.literal: His fame suddenly weighed heavily for a time.
translations.idiomatic: For a time his reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 初，秩隱居，既不肯仕，世以為必退者也。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhi lived in seclusion and refused office, the world took him for one who would surely decline.
translations.idiomatic: At first, while Zhi lived in seclusion and refused office, everyone assumed he would never serve.

sentences.zh: 後安石為相更法，天下沸騰，以為不便，秩在閭閻，見所下令，獨以為是，一召遂起。

translations.literal: Later, when Anshi became chief minister and changed the laws, the realm seethed and thought it harmful; Zhi in his lane, seeing the orders issued, alone thought them right, and at one summons he rose.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Anshi became chief minister and reformed the laws, the empire boiled with opposition; Zhi at home, reading the new orders, alone approved them, and answered a single summons to office.

sentences.zh: 在朝廷任諫爭，為侍從，低首抑氣，無所建明，聞望日損，為時譏笑。

translations.literal: At court he bore remonstrance and served in the inner entourage, bowing his head and suppressing his spirit, making no clear proposals; his reputation daily declined and contemporaries mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: At court he held remonstrance posts and served close to the throne, but bowed low and held his tongue, advancing nothing of note; his standing dwindled and people laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 秩長於《春秋》，至斥孫復所學為不近人情。

translations.literal: Zhi excelled in the Spring and Autumn Annals and even denounced Sun Fu's learning as remote from human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was expert in the Spring and Autumn Annals and even dismissed Sun Fu's scholarship as inhumane.

sentences.zh: 著講解數十篇，自謂「聖人之道，皆在於是」。

translations.literal: He wrote several tens of expository essays and claimed that "the way of the sages is all in these."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote dozens of commentaries and declared that the way of the sages lay entirely in them.

sentences.zh: 及安石廢《春秋》，遂盡諱其學。

translations.literal: When Anshi abolished the Spring and Autumn Annals, he then wholly concealed that learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi discarded the Spring and Autumn Annals, Zhi hid that scholarship entirely.

sentences.zh: 立，始命為天平軍推官，秩死，使門人趙冲狀其行，云：「自秩與安石去位，天下官吏陰變其法，民受塗炭，上下循默，敗端內萌，莫覺莫悟。

translations.literal: Li, at first appointed military adjutant of the Tianping Army, after Zhi's death had his student Zhao Chong set forth his conduct, saying, "From the time Zhi and Anshi left office, officials throughout the realm secretly altered the laws and the people suffered ruin; above and below went along in silence while the seeds of defeat grew within, unnoticed and unawakened.
translations.idiomatic: Li, first named adjutant of the Tianping Army, after Zhi's death had his student Zhao Chong draft a conduct report saying that once Zhi and Anshi left office, officials everywhere quietly undermined the reforms and the people were ruined; court and country stayed silent while defeat ripened within, unseen and unheeded.

sentences.zh: 秩知其必敗。」

translations.literal: Zhi knew it would certainly fail."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had known the policy was doomed."

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，蔡卞薦立為秘書省正字、諸王府說書侍講，請用為崇政殿說書，得召對，又請以為諫官。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng era Cai Bian recommended Li as Regular Scribe of the Secretariat and Lecturer in the Princes' Establishment, asked that he be used as Lecturer at the Hall of Exalted Governance, obtained an audience, and again asked that he be made remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaosheng period Cai Bian recommended Li as regular scribe of the Secretariat and lecturer in the princes' establishment, sought his appointment as lecturer at the Hall of Exalted Governance, secured an audience, and again asked that he be made a remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 卞方與章惇比，曾布欲傾之，乘間為哲宗言立附兩人，因暴其行狀事，以為詆毀先帝。

translations.literal: Bian was then aligned with Zhang Dun; Zeng Bu wished to topple him and, seizing an opportunity, told the Zhezong Emperor that Li sided with both men and exposed the conduct report affair as slandering the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was then allied with Zhang Dun; Zeng Bu tried to bring him down and told Zhezong that Li had sided with both men, exposing the conduct report as an attack on the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝亟下史院取視，言其不遜，以責惇、卞，惇、卞懼，請貶立，乃黜監永州酒稅。

translations.literal: The emperor quickly sent to the History Academy to view it, said it was disrespectful, and rebuked Dun and Bian; Dun and Bian were afraid and asked that Li be demoted, so he was banished to supervise the wine tax at Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered the History Academy to produce the text, called it insolent, and rebuked Dun and Bian; frightened, they asked that Li be demoted, and he was sent to supervise the wine tax at Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鄧綰，字文約，成都雙流人。

translations.literal: Deng Wan, styled Wenyue, was a native of Shuangliu in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan, who styled himself Wenyue, came from Shuangliu in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為禮部第一。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and ranked first in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and placed first in the Ministry of Rites competition.

sentences.zh: 稍遷職方員外郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to vice director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年冬，通判寧州。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Xining he was made vice prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Xining he was appointed vice prefect of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時王安石得君專政，條上時政數十事，以為宋興百年，習安玩治，當事更化。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Anshi had won the ruler's trust and monopolized government, itemizing several tens of affairs of the time and holding that since the Song had risen for a century and grown accustomed to ease and playful governance, those in charge must change and transform.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi then held the emperor's trust and dominated policy, listing dozens of reforms and arguing that after a century of Song rule grown soft with ease, those in power had to transform the state.

sentences.zh: 又上書言：「陛下得伊、呂之佐，作青苗、免役等法，民莫不歌舞聖澤。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty has obtained assistants like Yi Yin and Lü Shang and has enacted laws such as the Green Sprouts and Exemption from Corvée; the people all sing of the sage's grace.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote that the emperor had ministers like Yi Yin and Lü Shang and had enacted the Green Sprouts and corvée-exemption laws, so that the people everywhere praised imperial benevolence.

sentences.zh: 以臣所見寧州觀之，知一路皆然；

translations.literal: Judging from what I have seen in Ning Prefecture, I know it is the same throughout the circuit;
translations.idiomatic: From what I have seen in Ning Prefecture, I know the same holds for the whole circuit;

sentences.zh: 以一路觀之，知天下皆然。

translations.literal: judging from one circuit, I know it is the same throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: and from one circuit I know it is true for the entire empire.

sentences.zh: 誠不世之良法，願勿移於浮議而堅行之。」

translations.literal: Truly this is an unexampled excellent method; I pray you not shift it because of floating criticism but firmly carry it through."
translations.idiomatic: These are truly unmatched policies; do not let loose talk move you, but hold firm to them.

sentences.zh: 其辭蓋媚王安石。

translations.literal: His words were plainly flattering to Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was plainly designed to please Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 又貽以書頌，極其佞諛。

translations.literal: He also sent him a letter of praise, extreme in servile flattery.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Anshi a letter of praise steeped in sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 安石薦於神宗，驛召對。

translations.literal: Anshi recommended him to the Shenzong Emperor and he was summoned by express courier for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi recommended him to Shenzong, who summoned him by fast courier for an audience.

sentences.zh: 方慶州有夏寇，綰敷陳甚悉，帝問安石及呂惠卿，以不識對，帝曰：「安石，今之古人；

translations.literal: At the time there were Xia raiders in Qing Prefecture; Wan laid out the situation in great detail. The emperor asked Anshi and Lü Huizhang, who answered that they did not know him; the emperor said, "Anshi is a man of antiquity today;
translations.idiomatic: While Xia bandits troubled Qing Prefecture, Wan described the frontier in detail. The emperor asked Anshi and Lü Huizhang, who said they did not know him; the emperor said, "Anshi is the sage of our age;

sentences.zh: 惠卿，賢人也。」

translations.literal: Huizhang is a worthy man."
translations.idiomatic: Huizhang is a worthy man.

sentences.zh: 退見安石，欣然如素交。

translations.literal: On retiring he met Anshi and was delighted as if they had long been friends.
translations.idiomatic: After the audience he met Anshi and greeted him like an old friend.

sentences.zh: 宰相陳升之，馮京以綰練邊事，屬安石致齋，復使知寧州，綰聞之不樂，誦言：「急召我來，乃使還邪？」

translations.literal: The chief ministers Chen Shengzhi and Feng Jing, because Wan was versed in border affairs, asked Anshi to arrange an audience; he was again made to know Ning Prefecture. Wan heard this unhappily and said aloud, "You rush to summon me, then send me back?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Chen Shengzhi and Feng Jing, noting Wan's knowledge of frontier affairs, had Anshi arrange another audience and sent him back to Ning Prefecture. Wan was displeased and said, "You hurry me here only to send me back?"

sentences.zh: 或問：「君今當作何官？」

translations.literal: Someone asked, "What office will you hold now?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "What post will you get now?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不失為館職。」

translations.literal: He said, "At least a palace post."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "At least a post in the palace academies."

sentences.zh: 「得無為諫官乎？」

translations.literal: "Will you not become a remonstrance official?"
translations.idiomatic: "Surely not a remonstrance post?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「正自當爾。」

translations.literal: He said, "That is exactly how it should be."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "That is exactly what I should get."

sentences.zh: 明日，果除集賢校理、檢正中書孔目房。

translations.literal: The next day he was indeed made Collation Scholar of the Jixian Hall and Inspector of the Zhongshu Office of Miscellaneous Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was appointed collation scholar of the Jixian Hall and inspector of the Zhongshu office of miscellaneous accounts.

sentences.zh: 鄉人在都者皆笑且罵，綰曰：「笑罵從汝，好官須我為之。」

translations.literal: Fellow townsmen in the capital all laughed and cursed; Wan said, "Laugh and curse as you like—a good office still requires me to fill it."
translations.idiomatic: Townsmen in the capital laughed and cursed him; Wan said, "Mock me all you want—someone still has to take the good posts.

sentences.zh: 尋同知諫院。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Vice Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became vice director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 獻所著《洪範建極錫福論》，帝曰：「《洪範》，天人、自然之大法，朕方欲舉而措諸天下，矯革眾敝。

translations.literal: He presented his work "Discussion on Establishing the Ultimate and Bestowing Blessings from the Hongfan." The emperor said, "The Hongfan is the great law of Heaven and man and nature; I am just about to raise it and set it throughout the realm, correcting the many abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his treatise on the Hongfan's teaching of establishing the ultimate and bestowing blessings. The emperor said, "The Hongfan is the great natural law linking Heaven and humanity; I mean to enact it across the empire and sweep away abuses.

sentences.zh: 卿當堲淫朋比德之人，規以助朕。」

translations.literal: You should sternly regulate men who form factions and compare virtues, and advise me to help."
translations.idiomatic: You must curb faction-makers and men who band by affinity, and counsel me in the work."

sentences.zh: 綰頓首曰：「敢不力行所學，以奉聖訓。」

translations.literal: Wan kowtowed and said, "How dare I not forcefully practice what I have learned to serve the sage's instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Wan kowtowed and said, "I will do all I can to apply my learning to Your Majesty's teaching."

sentences.zh: 明年，遷侍御史知雜事、判司農寺。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to Supervising Censor with Concurrent Affairs and judge of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to supervising censor with concurrent duties and made judge of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時常平、水利、免役、保甲之政，皆出司農，故安石藉綰以威眾。

translations.literal: At that time the policies of the Ever-Normal Granary, water conservancy, corvée exemption, and militia organization all came from the Ministry of Revenue, so Anshi relied on Wan to awe the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-Normal Granary, waterworks, corvée exemption, and militia policies all issued from that ministry, and Anshi used Wan to intimidate opponents.

sentences.zh: 綰請先行免役於府界，次及諸道。

translations.literal: Wan asked that corvée exemption first be carried out in the metropolitan prefecture, then extended to the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Wan urged implementing corvée exemption first in the capital region, then in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 利州路歲用錢九萬六千緡，而轉運使李瑜率三十萬，綰言：「均役本以裕民，今乃務聚斂，積寬餘，宜加重黜。」

translations.literal: The Lizhou circuit used ninety-six thousand strings of cash yearly, but the transport commissioner Li Yu led thirty myriads; Wan said, "Equalizing corvée was meant to enrich the people, yet now they strive to amass levies and pile surpluses—he should be heavily demoted."
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou circuit needed ninety-six thousand strings a year, but transport commissioner Li Yu collected three hundred thousand; Wan said, "Corvée reform was meant to help the people, yet he hoards levies and surpluses—he deserves severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 富弼在亳，不散青苗錢，綰請付吏究治。

translations.literal: When Fu Bi was in Bo and would not distribute Green Sprouts money, Wan asked that officials be sent to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Bi in Bo refused to distribute Green Sprouts funds, Wan demanded an official inquiry.

sentences.zh: 畿縣民訴助役，詔詢其便否兩行之，綰與曾布輒上還堂帖。

translations.literal: When people in the capital counties complained about assisted corvée, an edict asked whether it was convenient or not and ordered both sides tried; Wan and Zeng Bu at once returned the office memorandum.
translations.idiomatic: When capital-county residents protested assisted corvée, the court asked whether the policy helped or hurt and ordered both views tried; Wan and Zeng Bu immediately returned the office slip unsigned.

sentences.zh: 中丞楊繪言未聞司農得繳奏者，不報。

translations.literal: The vice censor Yang Hui said he had never heard of the Ministry of Revenue withdrawing a memorial, and there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor Yang Hui said he had never known the ministry to recall a memorial unanswered, and nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 凡呂公著、謝景溫所置推直官、主簿，悉罷去之，而引蔡確、唐坰為御史。

translations.literal: All the investigating officials and clerks Lü Gongzhu and Xie Jingwen had appointed were dismissed, while Cai Que and Tang Kan were brought in as censors.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed every investigating officer and clerk Lü Gongzhu and Xie Jingwen had placed, and installed Cai Que and Tang Kan as censors.

sentences.zh: 五年春，擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he was made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 國朝故事，未有臺雜為中丞者，帝特命之。

translations.literal: By dynastic precedent no supervising censor with concurrent affairs had become censor-in-chief; the emperor specially appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Court precedent had never raised a supervising censor with concurrent duties to censor-in-chief; the emperor made an exception.

sentences.zh: 又加龍圖閣待制。

translations.literal: He was also given the additional title of Academician Awaiting Orders at the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made awaiting-orders academician at the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 建言：「頃時御史罷免，猶除省府職司，蓋厥初選用既審，則議論雖不合，人材亦不可遺，願籍前後諫官、御史得罪者姓名，以次甄錄，使於進退間與凡僚稍異，則思竭盡矣。」

translations.literal: He submitted a proposal: "In former times when censors were dismissed they were still given provincial and court posts, for if the initial selection was careful, then even when opinions did not agree talent should not be cast away; I pray you record the names of remonstrance officials and censors punished before and after in order and gradually select them, so that in advancement and dismissal they differ slightly from ordinary officials—then they will think to exhaust themselves."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that dismissed censors had once still received other posts because careful selection meant talent should not be wasted even when views clashed; he asked that punished remonstrance officials and censors be listed and gradually reappointed so promotion and demotion would differ from ordinary clerks and they would give their all.

sentences.zh: 遼人來理邊地，屯兵境上，聲言將用師，於是兩河戒嚴，且令河北修城守之具。

translations.literal: Khitan came to settle border lands, massed troops on the frontier, and declared they would use force; the two Hebei circuits were put on alert and Hebei was ordered to prepare walls and defense equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan came to dispute border territory, massed troops on the frontier, and threatened war; both Hebei circuits were alerted and ordered to ready fortifications.

sentences.zh: 綰曰：「非徒無益，且大擾費。」

translations.literal: Wan said, "Not only is it useless—it is greatly wasteful."
translations.idiomatic: Wan said, "It is not only useless but ruinously expensive.

sentences.zh: 帝從其言而止。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice and halted the work.

sentences.zh: 又言：「遼妄為地訟，意在窺我。

translations.literal: He also said, "The Khitan falsely raise land disputes intending to spy on us.
translations.idiomatic: He also said the Khitan invented border suits to probe the Song.

sentences.zh: 去冬聚兵累月，逡巡自罷，其情偽可見。

translations.literal: Last winter they gathered troops for months, then hesitated and withdrew on their own—their falsity can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: They had massed troops for months last winter, then drifted away—their bluff was obvious.

sentences.zh: 今當禦之以堅強，則不渝二國之平，平則彼不我疑，而我得以遠慮。

translations.literal: Now we should meet them with firm strength, then the peace between the two states will not be broken; if peace holds they will not suspect us and we can plan far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: China should answer with firm strength so the two-state peace holds; if peace holds they will not suspect us and we can plan ahead.

sentences.zh: 苟先之以畏屈，彼或將力爭，則大為中國之恥。」

translations.literal: If we first show fear and submission, they may strive in contention, and that will be a great shame for China."
translations.idiomatic: If we begin with fear and concession, they may press harder and China will suffer deep humiliation.

sentences.zh: 帝覽疏嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and commended it.

sentences.zh: 安石去位，綰頗附呂惠卿。

translations.literal: When Anshi left office, Wan largely attached himself to Lü Huizhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi left office, Wan largely sided with Lü Huizhang.

sentences.zh: 及安石復相，綰欲彌前跡，乃發惠卿置田華亭事，出知陳州。

translations.literal: When Anshi returned as chief minister, Wan wished to erase his earlier tracks and exposed Huizhang's affair of acquiring fields at Huating, so he was sent out to know Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi returned as chief minister, Wan tried to bury his old ties and exposed Huizhang's Huating land purchases, and was sent out as prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 又論三司使章惇協濟其奸，出知湖州。

translations.literal: He also charged the Commissioner of the Three Departments Zhang Dun with abetting his villainy and was sent out to know Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also accused Three Departments commissioner Zhang Dun of abetting the fraud and was transferred to Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，惠卿弟和卿創手實法，綰曰：「凡民養生之具，日用而家有之。

translations.literal: At first Huizhang's younger brother Heqing devised the household inventory law; Wan said, "All the people's means of sustaining life are things used daily and kept in the home.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Huizhang's brother Heqing had devised the household inventory law; Wan said, "Everything people need to live is what they use daily and keep at home.

sentences.zh: 今欲盡令疏實，則家有告訐之憂，人懷隱匿之慮，無所措手足矣。

translations.literal: Now if they are all forced to report in detail, then families will have the worry of informing on one another and people the anxiety of concealment, with nowhere to set hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing full disclosure would fill homes with mutual denunciation and people with fear of hiding things—they would have nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 商賈通殖貨財，交易有無，不過服食、器用、米粟、絲麻、布帛之類，或春有之而夏以蕩析，或秋貯之而冬已散亡，公家簿書，何由拘錄，其勢安得不犯？

translations.literal: Merchants circulate goods and wealth, trading what exists and what does not, no more than food, drink, utensils, rice, hemp, silk, and cloth; some have them in spring and by summer they are dispersed and dissolved, or stored in autumn and by winter already scattered and lost—how can the government's ledgers bind and record them? How could the situation fail to breed violations?
translations.idiomatic: Merchants only move food, clothing, grain, hemp, silk, and cloth; stock held in spring may be gone by summer, autumn stores may vanish by winter—official registers cannot track that without driving everyone into violation.

sentences.zh: 徒使嚚訟者趨賞報怨以相告訐，畏怯者守死忍困而已。」

translations.literal: It would only make the litigious rush for rewards to report grudges, while the timid would guard death and endure hardship."
translations.idiomatic: It would only send the quarrelsome to denounce enemies for reward while the timid suffered in silence."

sentences.zh: 詔罷其法。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished the law.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士，仍為中丞。

translations.literal: He was moved to Hanlin Academician, still serving as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician while remaining censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 綰慮安石去失勢，乃上言宜錄安石子及婿，仍賜第京師。

translations.literal: Wan feared that if Anshi left he would lose power and submitted that Anshi's son and son-in-law should be recorded and given mansions in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing loss of influence if Anshi fell, Wan urged recording Anshi's son and son-in-law and granting them houses in the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝以語安石，安石曰：「綰為國司直，而為宰臣乞恩澤，極傷國體，當黜。」

translations.literal: The emperor spoke of this to Anshi; Anshi said, "Wan serves the state with integrity yet begs favors for a chief minister—this gravely injures the body politic and he should be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Anshi, who said, "Wan holds a state post yet begs private favors for a chief minister—that wounds the state and he should be removed.

sentences.zh: 又薦彭汝礪為御史，安石不悅，遽自劾失舉。

translations.literal: He also recommended Peng Yulü as censor; Anshi was displeased and hastily impeached himself for a bad recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Peng Yulü as censor; Anshi was angry and at once impeached himself for poor judgment.

sentences.zh: 帝謂綰操心頗僻，賦性奸回，論事薦人，不循分守，斥知虢州。

translations.literal: The emperor said Wan's mind was rather perverse, his nature treacherous and crooked, that in discussing affairs and recommending people he did not keep to his station, and dismissed him to know Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Wan's mind crooked and his nature deceitful, said he overstepped his role in debate and patronage, and sent him out as prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，為集賢院學士、知河陽，元豐中，以待制知荊南、陳、陝，徙永興軍，改青州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was made Academician of the Jixian Hall and prefect of Heyang; in the Yuanfeng era he successively knew Jingnan, Chen, and Shan, was moved to the Yongxing Army, and then to Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was academician of the Jixian Hall and prefect of Heyang; under Yuanfeng he governed Jingnan, Chen, and Shan, then Yongxing, then Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 奏言歲大稔，斗粟五七錢。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the year was greatly abundant and a dou of grain cost five or seven cash.
translations.idiomatic: He reported a bumper harvest with grain at five to seven cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 帝知其佞，令提舉官酌市價以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor knew he was servile and ordered the supervising official to set market price and report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew he was flattering and told supervisors to check market prices and report.

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣直學士、知鄧州。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Deng.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，徙揚州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was moved to Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou he was transferred to Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 言者論其奸，改滁州，未去鄧而卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: Remonstrators charged his treachery; he was changed to Chu Prefecture and died in Deng before he left, at fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Critics denounced his treachery; he was reassigned to Chu but died in Deng at fifty-nine before he left.

sentences.zh: 子：洵仁、洵武。

translations.literal: Sons: Xunren and Xunwu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xunren and Xunwu.

sentences.zh: 洵仁，大觀中為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Xunren, in the Daguan era, was Vice Director of the Ministry of Works on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Xunren became right vice minister of works in the Daguan period.

sentences.zh: 子 洵武

translations.literal: Son: Xunwu.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xunwu.

sentences.zh: 洵武，字子常，第進士，為汝陽簿。

translations.literal: Xunwu, styled Zichang, passed the jinshi examination and was made clerk of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xunwu, who styled himself Zichang, earned the jinshi degree and served as clerk of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng era.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaosheng period.

sentences.zh: 哲宗召對，為秘書省正字、校書郎、國史院編修官，撰《神宗史》，議論專右蔡卞，詆誣宣仁后尤切，史禍之作，其力居多。

translations.literal: The Zhezong Emperor summoned him for an audience and made him Regular Scribe of the Secretariat, Collator, and Compiler at the National History Academy, compiling the "History of the Shenzong Emperor"; his arguments consistently favored Cai Bian, and he slandered Empress Dowager Xuanren with especial bitterness—the making of the history disaster owed much to his force.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong called him to court, appointed him regular scribe, collator, and national-history compiler, and put him to work on the History of Shenzong; he consistently backed Cai Bian and viciously defamed Empress Dowager Xuanren, and the great history scandal owed much to his efforts.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was moved to Attendant of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，改秘書少監，既而用蔡京薦，復史職，御史陳次升、陳師錫言：「洵武父綰在熙寧時以曲媚王安石，神宗數其邪僻奸回，今置洵武太史，豈能公心直筆，發揚神考之盛德，而不掩其父之惡乎？

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huizong reign he was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat; soon, on Cai Jing's recommendation, he resumed history duties. Censors Chen Cisheng and Chen Shixi said: "Xunwu's father Wan in the Xining era curried favor with Wang Anshi; the Shenzong Emperor repeatedly called him perverse and treacherous—now placing Xunwu as Grand Historian, how can he write with an impartial brush, exalt the late emperor's great virtue, and not cover his father's crimes?
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huizong's reign he became vice director of the Secretariat, then on Cai Jing's recommendation returned to history work. Censors Chen Cisheng and Chen Shixi argued that Wan had flattered Wang Anshi in Xining and that Shenzong had often called him crooked—how could his son as grand historian write fairly, praise Shenzong's virtue, and still hide his father's sins?

sentences.zh: 且其人材凡近，學問荒繆，不足以汙此選。」

translations.literal: Moreover his talent is mediocre and his learning crude and absurd—not enough to stain this selection."
translations.idiomatic: They added that his talent was mediocre and his scholarship shoddy, unworthy of the post.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時韓忠彥、曾布為相，洵武因對言：「陛下乃先帝子，今相忠彥乃琦之子。

translations.literal: At the time Han Zhongyan and Zeng Bu were chief ministers; Xunwu took advantage of an audience to say: "Your Majesty is the late emperor's son, while the chief minister Zhongyan is Qi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhongyan and Zeng Bu were then chief ministers; Xunwu told the emperor that Huizong was Shenzong's son while Zhongyan was Han Qi's son.

sentences.zh: 先帝行新法以利民，琦嘗論其非，今忠彥為相，更先帝之法，是忠彥能繼父志，陛下為不能也。

translations.literal: The late emperor enacted new laws to benefit the people; Qi once criticized them as wrong—now Zhongyan as chief minister changes the late emperor's laws, so Zhongyan can continue his father's will but Your Majesty cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong's new laws had helped the people, yet Qi had attacked them; now Zhongyan as chief minister reversed those laws, so Zhongyan could follow his father's wishes but the emperor could not.

sentences.zh: 必欲繼志述事，非用蔡京不可。」

translations.literal: If you must continue his will and carry on his work, none but Cai Jing will do."
translations.idiomatic: If the throne truly meant to continue Shenzong's work, only Cai Jing would suffice.

sentences.zh: 京出居外鎮，帝未有意復用也，洵武為帝言：「陛下方紹述先志，群臣無助者。」

translations.literal: Jing was out governing an outer command; the emperor had not yet intended to reuse him, but Xunwu told the emperor: "Your Majesty is just now continuing the late emperor's will, yet among the ministers there is no helper."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing was serving in the provinces and Huizong had not planned to recall him, but Xunwu said the court lacked anyone to help carry on Shenzong's legacy.

sentences.zh: 乃作《愛莫助之圖》以獻。

translations.literal: He then made the "Chart of Beloved but Unhelped" and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He then drew up and presented his Chart of Beloved but Unhelped.

sentences.zh: 其圖如《史記》年表，列旁行七重，別為左右，左曰元豐，右曰元祐，自宰相、執政、侍從、臺諫、郎官、館閣、學校各為一重。

translations.literal: The chart resembled the chronological tables of the "Records of the Grand Historian," with seven lateral rows divided left and right: left labeled Yuanfeng, right labeled Yuanyou; from chief ministers and administrators through attendants, remonstrance officials, bureau gentlemen, academy posts, and schools, each formed one row.
translations.idiomatic: The chart copied the Shiji annal tables with seven side-by-side ranks, left for Yuanfeng and right for Yuanyou, listing everyone from chief ministers and administrators through remonstrance officials, clerks, academicians, and school officers.

sentences.zh: 左序助紹述者，執政中唯溫益一人，餘不過三四，若趙挺之、范致虛、王能甫、錢遹之屬而已。

translations.literal: The left listed those who aided continuation of the policy; among administrators only Wen Yi stood alone, the rest no more than three or four such as Zhao Tingzhi, Fan Zhixu, Wang Nengfu, and Qian Yuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The left column named supporters of Shenzong's legacy—only Wen Yi among administrators, plus a handful like Zhao Tingzhi, Fan Zhixu, Wang Nengfu, and Qian Yuzhi.

sentences.zh: 右序舉朝輔相、公卿、百執事咸在，以百數，帝出示曾布，而揭去左方一姓名，布請之，帝曰：「蔡京也。

translations.literal: The right listed the whole court's assisting ministers, dukes, and the hundred offices—all there, numbering in the hundreds. The emperor showed it to Zeng Bu but peeled off one name on the left; Bu asked for it and the emperor said: "Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The right column packed in scores of ministers and officials. Huizong showed the chart to Zeng Bu but removed one name from the left; when Bu asked who it was, the emperor said, Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 洵武謂非相此人不可，以與卿不同，故去之。」

translations.literal: Xunwu said none but this man could be chief minister; because he differed from you, the name was removed."
translations.idiomatic: Xunwu insisted only Cai Jing could be chief minister and had removed the name because it disagreed with Bu.

sentences.zh: 布曰：「洵武既與臣所見異，臣安敢豫議？」

translations.literal: Bu said: "Since Xunwu's view differs from mine, how dare I take part in deliberation?"
translations.idiomatic: Bu replied that if Xunwu disagreed with him he dared not join the discussion.

sentences.zh: 明日改付溫益，益欣然奉行，請籍異論者，於是決意相京。

translations.literal: The next day it was handed to Wen Yi; Yi gladly carried it out and asked to register dissenters, and thus the decision to make Jing chief minister was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the task went to Wen Yi, who eagerly compiled lists of dissenters, and the court resolved to appoint Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 進洵武中書舍人、給事中兼侍講，修撰《哲宗實錄》，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Xunwu was advanced to Secretariat Drafter, Gentlemen Attendant, and Concurrent Lecturer, compiled the "Veritable Records of the Zhezong Emperor," and was moved to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Xunwu rose to secretariat drafter, gentlement attendant, and concurrent lecturer, helped compile Zhezong's veritable records, and became vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 洵武疏言：「神宗稽古建官，既正省、臺、寺、監之職，而以寄祿階易空名矣。

translations.literal: Xunwu submitted that "the Shenzong Emperor examined antiquity to establish offices, already correcting the duties of departments, bureaus, directorates, and commissions, while using nominal salary ranks to replace empty titles.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Shenzong had reorganized the bureaucracy and replaced hollow titles with salary ranks.

sentences.zh: 今在選七階，自兩使判官至主簿、尉，有帶知安州雲夢縣而為河東幹當公事者，有河中司錄參軍而監楚州鹽場者，有瀛州軍事推官、知大名府元城縣充濮州教授者，殽亂紛錯，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: Now among the seven ranks in selection, from the two commissioners and acting prefects down to chief clerks and constables, some bear acting knowledge of Yunmeng County in An Prefecture while serving as commissary affairs officer in Hedong; some are recorder of Hezhong while supervising the Chu Prefecture salt works; some are military adjutant of Ying Prefecture and magistrate of Yuancheng in Daming while filling the post of professor at Pu Prefecture—confusion and disorder, nothing worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: He complained that clerks now juggled absurd combinations of posts—Anzhou magistrates doing Hedong errands, Hezhong recorders running salt pans, Yingzhou adjutants teaching in Pu—creating hopeless confusion.

sentences.zh: 謂宜造為新名，因而制祿。」

translations.literal: He said new names should be devised and salaries regulated accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He urged new titles and matching salaries.

sentences.zh: 詔悉更之。

translations.literal: An edict wholly changed them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict overhauled the system.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，又請初出官人兼用刑法試，俾知為吏之方。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of Justice and also asked that new entrants to office be tested in penal law so they would know the ways of being officials.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to minister of justice, he also demanded penal-law exams for new officials.

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，拜尚書右丞，轉左丞、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning he was made Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, then Left Vice Director and Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning's third year he became right vice minister of works, then left vice minister and secretariat vice director.

sentences.zh: 妖人張懷素獄興，其黨有與洵武連昏者，坐出知隨州。

translations.literal: When the case of the sorcerer Zhang Huaisu arose, among his party were some connected by marriage to Xunwu; he was punished by being sent out to know Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhang Huaisu sorcery case broke, associates linked to Xunwu by marriage implicated him and he was sent out to govern Sui.

sentences.zh: 提舉明道宮，復端明殿學士，知亳州、河南府，召為中太一宮使，連進觀文殿學士，為大名尹。

translations.literal: Put in charge of the Mingdao Palace, restored as Academician of the Duanming Hall, he knew Bo and Henan prefectures, was recalled as Commissioner of the Central Great Unity Palace, was successively advanced to Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, and became prefect of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: After overseeing the Mingdao Palace and serving as Duanming academician in Bo and Henan, he returned as commissioner of the Central Great Unity Palace, rose to viewing-literature academician, and governed Daming.

sentences.zh: 政和中，夏祭，入侍祠。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era, at the summer sacrifice he entered to attend the rites.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenghe he attended the summer imperial sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 以佑神觀使兼侍讀留修國史，改保大軍節度使。

translations.literal: As Commissioner of the You-Shen Observatory with Concurrent Lecturer he remained to compile the national history and was changed to Military Commissioner of the Baoda Army.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed on as You-Shen observatory commissioner and concurrent lecturer to edit the national history, then became Baoda military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知樞密院。

translations.literal: Before long he knew the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he headed the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五谿蠻擾邊，即仿陝西弓箭手製，募邊民習知溪洞險易者，置所司教以戰陣，勸以耕牧，得勝兵幾萬人以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: When the Five Streams Miao disturbed the border, he imitated the Shaanxi archer militia system, recruited border people skilled in the gorges' terrain, set offices to teach battle formations, encouraged farming and herding, and obtained nearly ten thousand seasoned troops to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When Five Streams Miao raided the frontier, he copied the Shaanxi archer-militia model, recruited locals who knew the ravines, trained them to fight and farm, and fielded nearly ten thousand veterans to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 遷特進，拜少保，封莘國公，恩典如宰相。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Exceptional Promotion, made Junior Guardian, enfeoffed as Duke of Xin, with favors like a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: He received exceptional promotion, became junior guardian, was enfeoffed Duke of Xin, and enjoyed privileges equal to a chief minister's.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，薨，年六十五，贈太傅，諡曰文簡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe he died at sixty-five; he was posthumously given Grand Tutor and the posthumous title Wénjiǎn.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanhe he died at sixty-five, posthumously honored as grand tutor with the temple name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 鄧氏自綰以來，世濟其奸，而洵武阿二蔡尤力。

translations.literal: From Wan onward the Deng clan for generations carried on treachery, while Xunwu toadied to the two Cais with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: From Wan's day the Dengs bred treachery through the generations, and Xunwu flattered the two Cais harder than any.

sentences.zh: 京之敗亂天下，禍源自洵武起焉。

translations.literal: Jing's ruin and disorder of the realm—the calamity began with Xunwu.
translations.idiomatic: The catastrophe of Cai Jing's ruin of the empire began with Xunwu.

sentences.zh: 李定，字資深，揚州人。

translations.literal: Li Ding, styled Zishen, was a native of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ding, who styled himself Zishen, came from Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少受學於王安石。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，為定遠尉、秀州判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was made Wei of Dingyuan and judge of Xiu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as constable of Dingyuan and judge of Xiu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，孫覺薦之，召至京師，謁諫官李常，常問曰：「君從南方來，民謂青苗法何如？」

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, Sun Jue recommended him; summoned to the capital, he visited remonstrance official Li Chang. Chang asked, "You come from the south—what do the people say of the Green Sprouts law?"
translations.idiomatic: In Xining's second year Sun Jue recommended him; summoned to court, he called on remonstrance official Li Chang, who asked what southerners thought of the Green Sprouts policy.

sentences.zh: 定曰：「民便之，無不喜者。」

translations.literal: Ding said, "The people find it convenient; none dislike it."
translations.idiomatic: Ding said the people welcomed it and no one complained.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「舉朝方共爭是事，君勿為此言。」

translations.literal: Chang said, "The whole court is debating this matter—do not speak thus."
translations.idiomatic: Chang warned that the whole court was debating the policy and he should not say that.

sentences.zh: 定即往白安石，且曰：「定但知據實以言，不知京師乃不許。」

translations.literal: Ding at once went to inform Anshi and said, "Ding only knows to speak according to fact—I did not know the capital forbids it."
translations.idiomatic: Ding went straight to Anshi and said he had only reported what he saw and had not known the capital forbade such talk.

sentences.zh: 安石大喜，謂曰：「君且得見，盍為上道之。」

translations.literal: Anshi was greatly pleased and said, "You will soon have an audience—why not tell the emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was delighted and told him to repeat it to the emperor at audience.

sentences.zh: 立薦對。

translations.literal: He immediately recommended him for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: He at once secured him an audience.

sentences.zh: 神宗問青苗事，其對如曩言，於是諸言新法不便者，帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: The Shenzong Emperor asked about Green Sprouts; his reply was as before, and thereafter all who said the new laws were inconvenient—the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong asked about Green Sprouts; Ding answered as before, and from then on Shenzong ignored critics of the reforms.

sentences.zh: 命定知諫院，宰相言前無選人除諫官之比，遂拜太子中允、監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: He was ordered to know the Remonstrance Bureau; the chief ministers said there was no precedent for appointing a selection candidate as remonstrance official, so he was made Crown Prince Attendant and Supervising Censor in the Inner Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him into the Remonstrance Bureau; ministers noted no precedent for a selection candidate as remonstrator, so he became crown prince attendant and supervising censor in the inner bureau.

sentences.zh: 知制誥宋敏求、蘇頌、李大臨封還制書，皆罷去。

translations.literal: Drafting officials Song Minqiu, Su Song, and Li Dalin sealed and returned the appointment documents—all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting officials Song Minqiu, Su Song, and Li Dalin returned the appointment edicts sealed, and all were removed.

sentences.zh: 御史陳薦疏：「定頃為涇縣主簿，聞庶母仇氏死，匿不為服。」

translations.literal: Censor Chen Jian memorialized: "Ding once as chief clerk of Jing County, hearing his stepmother Lady Chou had died, concealed it and did not wear mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Jian charged that as Jing County clerk Ding had hidden his stepmother Lady Chou's death and refused mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔下江東、淮、浙轉運使問狀，奏云：「定嘗以父年老，求歸侍養，不云持所生母服。」

translations.literal: An edict sent the Jiangdong, Huai, and Zhe transport commissioners to investigate; they reported: "Ding once, because his father was old, asked to return to serve him in support, and did not speak of wearing mourning for his birth mother."
translations.idiomatic: Investigators reported that Ding had left office to care for his aged father and had never mentioned mourning for Lady Chou.

sentences.zh: 定自辯言，實不知為仇所生，故疑不敢服，而以侍養解官。

translations.literal: Ding defended himself, saying he truly did not know he was born of Chou, so he doubted and dared not mourn, and used supporting his father as the reason to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Ding claimed he had not known Chou was his birth mother, had feared to mourn wrongly, and had resigned to nurse his father.

sentences.zh: 曾公亮謂定當追行服，安石力主之，改為崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang said Ding should be made to observe mourning retroactively; Anshi strongly backed him, and he was changed to Lecturer at the Hall of Exalted Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang said Ding must mourn retroactively; Anshi overruled critics and made him lecturer at the Hall of Exalted Governance.

sentences.zh: 御史林旦、薛昌朝言，不宜以不孝之人居勸講之地，並論安石，章六七上，安石又白罷兩人，定亦不自安，蘄解職，以集賢校理、檢正中書吏房、直舍人院同判太常寺。

translations.literal: Censors Lin Dan and Xue Changchao said an unfilial man should not occupy a place of exhortation and lecturing, and together impeached Anshi in six or seven memorials; Anshi again had the two dismissed. Ding also felt uneasy and begged to leave office, becoming Collation Scholar of the Jixian Hall, Inspector of the Zhongshu Clerical Office, and Concurrent Judge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Lin Dan and Xue Changchao protested that an unfilial man should not lecture the throne and impeached Anshi repeatedly; Anshi had them dismissed. Uneasy himself, Ding sought relief as Jixian collator, Zhongshu clerical inspector, and concurrent judge of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 八年，加集賢殿修撰、知明州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was given Concurrent Compiler at the Hall of Cultivated Talents and made to know Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became compiler at the Hall of Cultivated Talents and prefect of Ming.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，召拜寶文閣待制、同知諫院，進知制誥，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng he was summoned and appointed Academician Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Treasured Writings and Vice Director of the Remonstrance Bureau, advanced to Drafting Official, and made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng he was recalled as treasured-writings academician and vice remonstrance director, then drafting official and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 劾蘇軾《湖州謝上表》，擿其語以為侮慢，因論軾自熙寧以來，作為文章，怨謗君父，交通戚里。

translations.literal: He impeached Su Shi's "Thanksgiving Memorial from Huzhou," plucking phrases as disrespect; he further argued that since Xining Shi had written works venting resentment and slandering ruler and father and trafficking with imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Su Shi's Huzhou thank-you memorial as insolent and claimed that since Xining Su had written pieces that slandered the throne and courted imperial relatives.

sentences.zh: 逮赴臺獄窮治，當會赦，論不已，竄之黃州。

translations.literal: He was sent to the Censorate for full investigation; when an amnesty was due he argued without cease and had him banished to Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Su was jailed and investigated; though an amnesty neared, Ding kept arguing until Su was exiled to Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 方定自鞫軾獄，勢不可回。

translations.literal: Just then Ding was himself examining Shi's case; the momentum could not be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was prosecuting the case himself and would not relent.

sentences.zh: 一日，於崇政殿門外語同列曰：「蘇軾乃奇才也。」

translations.literal: One day outside the Gate of Exalted Governance he said to colleagues, "Su Shi is a rare talent."
translations.idiomatic: One day outside the Gate of Exalted Governance he told colleagues that Su Shi was a rare talent.

sentences.zh: 俱不敢對。

translations.literal: None dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 請復六案糾察之職，並諸路監司皆得鉤考，從之。

translations.literal: He asked to restore the six-section inspection duty and that circuit supervisory commissioners all be allowed to audit—approved.
translations.idiomatic: He restored six-section inspection powers and let circuit supervisors conduct audits, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 彗出東方，求直言，太史謂有兵變，帝命宦者視衛士飲食。

translations.literal: When a comet appeared in the east the emperor sought blunt counsel; the grand astrologer said there would be military upheaval, and the emperor ordered eunuchs to inspect the guards' food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: After a comet appeared in the east, the grand astrologer warned of mutiny and the emperor sent eunuchs to inspect guards' rations.

sentences.zh: 定言一飯不足市恩，適起小人之心，乃止。

translations.literal: Ding said one meal was not enough to buy favor and would only stir petty minds, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said a single meal could not buy loyalty and would only breed suspicion, and the inspections ended.

sentences.zh: 或議廢明堂祀，帝以訪定。

translations.literal: Some debated abolishing the Bright Hall sacrifice; the emperor consulted Ding.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed canceling the Bright Hall rite, the emperor asked Ding.

sentences.zh: 定曰：「三歲一郊或明堂，祖宗以來，未之有改。

translations.literal: Ding said, "Sacrifice at the suburban altar every three years or at the Bright Hall—since the ancestors, there has been no change.
translations.idiomatic: Ding replied that triennial suburban or Bright Hall sacrifice had never changed since the founders.

sentences.zh: 誰為此言，願治其妄。」

translations.literal: Who speaks such words—I pray he be punished for his rashness."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever suggested abolition deserved punishment for recklessness.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「聽卿言足矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Hearing your words is enough."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Ding's word was enough.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was moved to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 坐論府界養馬事失實，罷知河陽，留守南京，召為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because his discussion of the metropolitan horse-raising affair was untrue, he was dismissed to know Heyang, remained to guard Nanjing, and was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After misreporting metropolitan horse policy he was sent to Heyang, guarded Nanjing, then recalled as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，以龍圖閣學士知青州，移江寧府。

translations.literal: When the Zhezong Emperor ascended the throne he was made Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qing Prefecture, then moved to Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhezong he became dragon-diagram academician and Qing prefect, then Jiangning prefect.

sentences.zh: 言者爭暴其前過，又謫居滁州。

translations.literal: Remonstrators vied to expose his former faults; he was again demoted to live in Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Critics exposed his old crimes and he was demoted to Chu.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanyou's second year.

sentences.zh: 定於宗族有恩，分財振贍，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: Ding was kind to his clan, divided wealth and gave relief, and his house had no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was generous to kin, shared his wealth, and left nothing behind.

sentences.zh: 得任子，先及兄息。

translations.literal: When he obtained a yin privilege for an official son, he gave it first to his elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: When he earned a yin privilege for a son, he gave it to his nephew first.

sentences.zh: 死之日，諸子皆布衣。

translations.literal: On the day he died all his sons wore common cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his sons wore only plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 徒以附王安石驟得美官，又陷蘇軾於罪，是以公論惡之，而不孝之名遂著。

translations.literal: He only because he attached to Wang Anshi suddenly obtained fine offices, and again trapped Su Shi in crime—therefore public opinion hated him, and the name of unfilial son became fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Because he clung to Wang Anshi for rapid promotion and destroyed Su Shi, public opinion despised him and his unfilial reputation stuck.

sentences.zh: 舒亶，字信道，明州慈溪人。

translations.literal: Shu Dan, styled Xindao, was a native of Cixi in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Dan, who styled himself Xindao, came from Cixi in Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 試禮部第一，調臨海尉。

translations.literal: He ranked first in the Ministry of Rites examination and was assigned as Wei of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the Ministry of Rites exam and became constable of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 民使酒詈逐後母，至亶前，命執之，不服，即自起斬之，投劾去。

translations.literal: A man made drunk and cursed his stepmother; brought before Dan, he refused to submit; Dan at once rose and beheaded him, then submitted an impeachment of himself and left office.
translations.idiomatic: When a drunk cursed his stepmother before Dan, the man resisted arrest; Dan stood, beheaded him, impeached himself, and resigned.

sentences.zh: 王安石當國，聞而異之，御史張商英亦稱其材，用為審官院主簿。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held the state, hearing of this he marveled; Censor Zhang Shangying also praised his talent, and he was used as Chief Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi, hearing of it, was impressed; Zhang Shangying praised him too, and he became chief clerk of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 使熙河括田，有績，遷奉禮郎。

translations.literal: Sent to the Xihe circuit to survey fields, he had achievement and was moved to Gentleman for Court Ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying fields on the Xihe frontier, he performed well and was promoted to gentleman for court ceremony.

sentences.zh: 鄭俠既貶，復被逮，亶承命往捕，遇諸陳。

translations.literal: After Zheng Xia was demoted he was seized again; Dan received orders to arrest him and met him on the road at several stations.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Xia was arrested again, Dan was ordered to seize him and intercepted him on the road.

sentences.zh: 搜俠篋，得所錄名臣諫草，有言新法事及親朋書尺，悉按姓名治之，竄俠嶺南，馮京、王安國諸人皆得罪。

translations.literal: Searching Xia's box, he obtained recorded remonstrance drafts of famous ministers, with matters on the new laws and letters among kin and friends; he prosecuted all by name, banished Xia to Lingnan, and Feng Jing, Wang Anguo, and others all suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Searching Zheng's chest he found remonstrance drafts and letters on the reforms and prosecuted everyone named, exiling Zheng to Lingnan and implicating Feng Jing, Wang Anguo, and others.

sentences.zh: 擢亶太子中允、提舉兩浙常平。

translations.literal: Dan was promoted to Crown Prince Attendant and put in charge of the two Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was made crown prince attendant and put in charge of the two Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，權監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng he was made Acting Supervising Censor in the Inner Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng he became acting supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 太學官受賂，事聞，亶奉詔驗治，凡辭語微及者，輒株連考竟，以多為功。

translations.literal: When bribery among Grand Academy officers was reported, Dan received orders to investigate; whatever words slightly touched on it he would implicate and examine to the end, taking multiplicity as achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When academy bribery surfaced, he was told to investigate and implicated anyone remotely connected, treating numbers as success.

sentences.zh: 加集賢校理。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Collation Scholar of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Jixian collation scholar.

sentences.zh: 同李定劾蘇軾作為歌詩議訕時事。

translations.literal: Together with Li Ding he impeached Su Shi for composing songs and poems that mocked current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Ding he impeached Su Shi for poems that mocked current affairs.

sentences.zh: 亶又言：「王詵輩公為朋比，如盛僑、周邠固不足論，若司馬光、張方平、范鎮、陳襄、劉摯，皆略能誦說先王之言，而所懷如此，可置而不誅乎？」

translations.literal: Dan also said, "Wang Shen and his sort openly form factions; men like Sheng Qiao and Zhou Bin are not worth discussion, but if Sima Guang, Zhang Fangping, Fan Zhen, Chen Xiang, and Liu Zhi can all recite the words of the former kings yet harbor such thoughts—can they be set aside and not punished?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan also claimed Wang Shen's clique was treasonous; lesser men did not matter, but Sima Guang, Zhang Fangping, Fan Zhen, Chen Xiang, and Liu Zhi, though they could quote the sages, harbored the same dissent—should they go unpunished?

sentences.zh: 帝覺其言為過，但貶軾、詵，而光等罰金。

translations.literal: The emperor felt his words excessive but only demoted Shi and Shen, while Guang and the rest were fined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought him excessive but only demoted Su and Wang Shen while fining the others.

sentences.zh: 未幾，同修起居注，改知諫院。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Concurrent Compiler of the Imperial Diary and changed to know the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he compiled the imperial diary and headed the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 張商英為中書檢正，遺亶手帖，示以子婿所為文。

translations.literal: Zhang Shangying as Zhongshu inspection commissioner sent Dan a personal note showing writings his son-in-law had done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shangying, as Zhongshu inspection commissioner, sent Dan a private note about his son-in-law's writings.

sentences.zh: 亶具以白，云商英為宰屬而干請言路，坐責監江陵稅。

translations.literal: Dan reported it in full, saying Shangying as a chief minister's subordinate was lobbying the remonstrance path, and was punished by supervising the Jiangling tax.
translations.idiomatic: Dan reported that a minister's aide was lobbying the remonstrance office and Zhang was demoted to supervise Jiangling tax.

sentences.zh: 始，亶以商英薦得用；

translations.literal: At first Dan had obtained use through Shangying's recommendation;
translations.idiomatic: Dan had originally risen on Zhang Shangying's recommendation;

sentences.zh: 及是，反陷之。

translations.literal: now he turned and trapped him.
translations.idiomatic: now he turned and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 進知雜御史、判司農寺，超拜給事中、權直學士院。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Supervising Censor with Concurrent Affairs and judge of the Ministry of Revenue, and in one month was made Gentlemen Attendant and Acting Academician of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He became supervising censor with concurrent duties and revenue judge, and within a month was gentlement attendant and acting academician.

sentences.zh: 逾月，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: After a month he was Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 舉劾多私，氣焰熏灼，見者側目，獨憚王安禮。

translations.literal: His impeachments were mostly private; his arrogance scorched—those who saw him glanced sideways; he alone feared Wang Anli.
translations.idiomatic: His indictments were mostly personal grudges; his arrogance blazed and men shrank from him, though he feared Wang Anli alone.

sentences.zh: 亶在翰林，受廚錢越法，三省以聞，事下大理。

translations.literal: When Dan was in the Hanlin Academy he received kitchen funds against regulation; the Three Departments reported it and the matter went down to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: As Hanlin academician he took kitchen funds illegally; the Three Departments reported him and the Court of Judicial Review took the case.

sentences.zh: 初，亶言尚書省凡奏鈔法當置籍，錄其事目。

translations.literal: At first Dan said that in the Secretariat every memorial slip law should have a register recording item headings.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had first argued that the Secretariat should keep registers of every memorial slip.

sentences.zh: 今違法不錄，既案奏，乃謾以發放曆為錄目之籍，亶以為大臣欺罔。

translations.literal: Now in violation of law they were not recorded; after the case was memorialized, they falsely used the disbursement ledger as the register of item headings—Dan held that the chief ministers had deceived.
translations.idiomatic: When officials failed to record them and then pretended disbursement ledgers were the register, Dan charged the chief ministers with fraud.

sentences.zh: 而尚書省取臺中受事籍驗之，亦無錄目，亶遽雜他文書送省，於是執政復發其欺。

translations.literal: The Secretariat took the Censorate's receipt register to verify it and also had no item headings; Dan hastily mixed other documents and sent them to the Secretariat, and then the administrators again exposed his deception.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat checked the Censorate receipt book and found no headings either; Dan then shuffled in other papers, and the administrators exposed his own deceit.

sentences.zh: 大理鞫廚錢事，謂亶為誤。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review examined the kitchen funds affair and said Dan had erred.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review ruled the kitchen-funds case a mistake.

sentences.zh: 法官吳外厚駁之，御史楊畏言亶所受文籍具在，無不承之理。

translations.literal: Judge Wu Waihou rebutted it; Censor Yang Wei said the documents Dan received were all present and there was no reason not to confess.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Wu Waihou objected; Censor Yang Wei said the records proved Dan's guilt beyond denial.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「亶自盜為贓，情輕而法重；

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Dan's self-theft is embezzlement—intent light but law heavy;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said self-theft was embezzlement—lighter in intent but heavier in law;

sentences.zh: 詐為錄目，情重而法輕。

translations.literal: falsifying the register—intent heavy but law light.
translations.idiomatic: falsifying registers was graver in intent though lighter in statute.

sentences.zh: 身為執法，而詐妄若是，安可置也！」

translations.literal: Holding office as law enforcer yet so deceitful—how can he be kept!"
translations.idiomatic: As a law officer he had lied so brazenly that he could not remain.

sentences.zh: 命追兩秩勒停。

translations.literal: He was ordered stripped of two ranks and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of two ranks and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 亶比歲起獄，好以疑似排抵士大夫，雖坐微罪廢斥，然遠近稱快。

translations.literal: Dan in recent years had raised cases and liked to use suspicion to strike down scholar-officials; though they sat for minor crimes and were dismissed, near and far rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: For years Dan had built cases on suspicion to ruin scholar-officials; even minor punishments delighted the public.

sentences.zh: 十餘年，始復通直郎。

translations.literal: After more than ten years he was at last restored as Master for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: Only after more than ten years was he restored as master for direct communication.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，知南康軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning he was made to know Nankang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongning he governed Nankang.

sentences.zh: 辰溪蠻叛，蔡京使知荊南，以開邊功，由直龍圖閣進待制，明年，卒，贈直學士。

translations.literal: When Chenxi Miao rebelled, Cai Jing sent him to know Jingnan to open frontier achievement; from Direct Dragon Diagram Hall he was advanced to Awaiting Orders, and the next year died, posthumously given Direct Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenxi Miao rebelled, Cai Jing sent him to Jingnan for frontier glory; promoted from direct dragon-diagram academician, he died the next year and was posthumously made direct academician.

sentences.zh: 蹇周輔

translations.literal: Jian Zhoufu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Zhoufu.

sentences.zh: 蹇周輔，字磻翁，成都雙流人。

translations.literal: Jian Zhoufu, styled Panyong, was a native of Shuangliu in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Zhoufu, who styled himself Panyong, came from Shuangliu in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 少與范鎮、何郯為布衣交。

translations.literal: In youth he and Fan Zhen and He Bin were friends as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he befriended Fan Zhen and He Bin while they were still commoners.

sentences.zh: 年未冠，試大廷，不第。

translations.literal: Before the cap, he tested in the great court and did not place.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he failed the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 鎮、郯既貴達，周輔始特奏名，再舉進士，知宜賓、石門二縣，通判安肅軍，為御史臺推直官。

translations.literal: After Fan and He had risen to honor, Zhoufu at last passed by special memorial and twice passed the jinshi, knew Yibin and Shimen counties, was vice prefect of the Ansu Army, and was investigating officer of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: After Fan and He rose high, Zhoufu finally passed by special presentation and twice earned the jinshi, governed Yibin and Shimen, served as Ansu vice prefect, and became a Censorate investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 善於訊鞫，鉤索微隱，皆用智得情。

translations.literal: Skilled at interrogation, he hooked and sought hidden subtleties and always obtained the facts by wit.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in interrogation, he traced hidden details until wit exposed the truth.

sentences.zh: 嘗有詔獄，事連掖庭掌寶侍史，它司累月不能決，乃命周輔。

translations.literal: Once there was an imperial prison case involving a palace attendant who kept the imperial treasures; other offices for months could not decide it, so Zhoufu was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Once an imperial case involving a palace treasure attendant stumped other offices for months until Zhoufu was assigned.

sentences.zh: 度不可追逮，奏請以要辭示主者詰服之，時以為知體。

translations.literal: Judging pursuit impossible, he memorialized asking to show essential phrases to the chief party to compel confession—at the time this was considered knowing propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing arrest was impossible, he asked to confront the chief suspect with key evidence to force confession, which contemporaries praised as proper procedure.

sentences.zh: 及治李逢獄竟，臺臣雜治無異辭，神宗稱其能，擢開封府推官，出為淮南轉運副使。

translations.literal: When the Li Feng case was concluded, censorial colleagues jointly tried it without differing words; the Shenzong Emperor praised his ability and promoted him to Push Officer of the Kaifeng Prefecture, then sent out as Vice Transport Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: After closing the Li Feng case to universal agreement, Shenzong praised his skill, made him Kaifeng push officer, then Huainan vice transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 盜廖恩聚黨閩中，多害兵吏，改使福建，護諸將以討之，恩遂降。

translations.literal: The bandit Liao En gathered a party in Fujian and harmed many soldiers and officials; he was changed to commissioner of Fujian to protect the generals in suppressing him, and En then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Liao En raided Fujian and killed soldiers and officials; reassigned to Fujian to direct suppression, Zhoufu accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，循唐制，歸百司獄於大理寺，選為少卿，遷三司度支副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng, following Tang practice, the hundred offices' prisons were returned to the Court of Judicial Review; he was selected as Vice Director and moved to Vice Commissioner of Revenue of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng, following Tang practice, agency prisons returned to the Court of Judicial Review; he became vice director, then vice revenue commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 先是，湖南例食淮鹽，周輔始請運廣鹽數百萬石，分鬻郴、全、道州；

translations.literal: Previously Hunan by custom ate Huai salt; Zhoufu first asked to transport several million shi of Guang salt to sell in Chen, Quan, and Dao prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Hunan had eaten Huai salt; Zhoufu first proposed shipping millions of shi of Guang salt to Chen, Quan, and Dao;

sentences.zh: 又以淮鹽增配潭、衡諸郡，湘中民愁困，法既行，遂領於度支。

translations.literal: he also increased Huai salt allotments to Tan and Heng prefectures—the people of central Hunan were distressed; once the law was enacted he then took charge at Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: he also increased Huai salt quotas in Tan and Heng, impoverishing central Hunan, then ran the policy from Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以集賢殿修撰為河北都轉運使，進寶文閣待制，召為戶部侍郎、知開封府，事多不決。

translations.literal: As Compiler at the Hall of Cultivated Talents he was made Metropolitan Transport Commissioner of Hebei, advanced to Academician Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Treasured Writings, summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue and to know Kaifeng Prefecture—many matters were not decided.
translations.idiomatic: As cultivated-talents compiler he became Hebei transport commissioner and treasured-writings academician, then vice minister of revenue and Kaifeng prefect, where he left many cases unsettled.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人，不拜，改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was given Secretariat Drafter but did not accept and was changed to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Offered secretariat drafter, he refused and became vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，言者暴其立江西、福建鹽法，掊克欺誕，負公擾民，罷知和州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou remonstrators exposed his establishing Jiangxi and Fujian salt laws, extortionate and deceitful, betraying the public and harassing the people—he was dismissed to know He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou critics exposed his Jiangxi and Fujian salt laws as extortionate fraud that betrayed the public, and he was sent to He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徙廬州。

translations.literal: He was moved to Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 周輔強學，善屬文，神宗嘗命作《答高麗書》，屢稱善。

translations.literal: Zhoufu studied forcefully and was skilled at composition; the Shenzong Emperor once ordered him to compose the "Reply to Goryeo" and repeatedly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: A forceful scholar and fine writer, he once drafted the Reply to Goryeo for Shenzong, who praised it repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 為吏深文刻覈，故老而獲戾。

translations.literal: As an official he applied the law in severe written detail, so in old age he incurred blame.
translations.idiomatic: As an official he wrote law harshly and narrowly, and in old age earned blame.

sentences.zh: 子序辰。

translations.literal: Son: Xuchen.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xuchen.

sentences.zh: 子 序辰

translations.literal: Son: Xuchen.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xuchen.

sentences.zh: 序辰，字授之，登第後數年，以泗州推官主管廣西常平。

translations.literal: Xuchen, styled Shouzhi, several years after passing the examination was made push officer of Si Prefecture in charge of Guangxi Ever-Normal Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Xuchen, who styled himself Shouzhi, years after passing the exam became Si push officer overseeing Guangxi Ever-Normal Granary.

sentences.zh: 周輔方使閩，上言父子並祗命遠方，家無所託，蘄改一近地。

translations.literal: Zhoufu was then commissioner in Fujian and submitted that father and son were both charged with distant commands with no home to rely on, and begged to change one to a nearer place.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhoufu served in Fujian, he begged to move his son nearer because father and son both held distant posts.

sentences.zh: 乃易京西，旋提舉江西常平，繼父行鹽法。

translations.literal: He was then changed to Jingxi, soon put in charge of Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granary, continuing his father's salt law.
translations.idiomatic: Xuchen was shifted to Jingxi, then put in charge of Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granary and continued his father's salt policy.

sentences.zh: 為監察御史，遷殿中侍御史、右司諫。

translations.literal: He was made Supervising Censor, moved to Palace Attending Censor and Right Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: He became supervising censor, then palace attending censor and right remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，改司封員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Zhezong Emperor ascended the throne he was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites for Seals.
