translations.idiomatic: Under Zhezong he became vice director of the ministry of rites for seals.

sentences.zh: 周輔得罪，以序辰成其惡，降簽書廬州判官。

translations.literal: When Zhoufu was punished, because Xuchen completed his evil he was demoted to Signing Secretary of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhoufu fell, Xuchen was demoted for completing his father's crimes to signing secretary of Lu.

sentences.zh: 起知楚州，提點江東刑獄。

translations.literal: He was raised to know Chu Prefecture and put in charge of judicial inspection in Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to Chu prefect and put in charge of Jiangdong judicial inspection.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，遷左司員外郎，進起居郎、中書舍人、同修國史。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng era he was moved to Left Department Vice Director, advanced to Attendant Gentleman, Secretariat Drafter, and Concurrent Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng he rose to left department vice director, attendant gentleman, secretariat drafter, and national-history compiler.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「朝廷前日正司馬光等奸惡，明其罪罰，以告中外。

translations.literal: He submitted: "The court formerly rectified the treachery and evil of Sima Guang and others, clarifying their crimes and punishments to inform inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the court had already punished Sima Guang and other traitors and should preserve the record.

sentences.zh: 惟變亂典刑，改廢法度，訕讟宗廟，睥睨兩宮，觀事考言，實狀彰著，然蹤跡深秘，包藏禍心，相去八年之間，蓋已不可究質。

translations.literal: Only in overturning canonical punishments, changing and abolishing laws, slandering the ancestral temple, and looking askance at the two palaces—in examining affairs and weighing words the facts are clearly manifest, yet traces are deeply hidden and treacherous hearts concealed; between spans of eight years investigation can no longer reach the substance.
translations.idiomatic: They had overturned law, slandered the ancestral temple, and eyed the two palaces; though guilt was clear, eight years made investigation impossible.

sentences.zh: 其章疏案牘，散在有司，若不彙緝而藏之，歲久必致淪棄。

translations.literal: Their memorials and case documents are scattered among offices; if not collected and stored, in time they will surely be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Their memorials and case papers were scattered among offices and would be lost without collection.

sentences.zh: 願悉討奸臣所言行，選官編類，入為一帙，置之一府，以示天下後世大戒。」

translations.literal: I pray you fully seek out what treacherous ministers did and said, select officials to compile by category into one volume, place it in one office, to show the great warning to the realm and posterity."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that treacherous ministers' acts be compiled into one volume as a warning to the realm and posterity.

sentences.zh: 遂命序辰及徐鐸編類。

translations.literal: He was then ordered with Xu Duo to compile by category.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him and Xu Duo to compile the files.

sentences.zh: 由是縉紳之禍，無一得脫者。

translations.literal: From this the calamity of gentry and officials—none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: From that project no Yuanyou official escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書，與安惇看詳訴理事。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of Rites and with An Dun examined appeal matters.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of rites and with An Dun reviewed appeals.

sentences.zh: 以奉使遼國無狀，黜知黃州。

translations.literal: Because his mission to Liao was disorderly he was demoted to know Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After misconduct on a Liao mission he was demoted to Huang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 閱四月，除龍圖閣待制、知揚州。

translations.literal: After four months he was made Academician Awaiting Orders at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Four months later he became dragon-diagram academician and Yang prefect.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，中書言序辰類元祐章牘，傅致語言，指為謗訕。

translations.literal: When the Huizong Emperor ascended the throne the Secretariat said Xuchen had classified Yuanyou memorials, fabricating language and calling it slander.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong's secretariat said Xuchen had twisted Yuanyou memorials into slander.

sentences.zh: 詔與惇並除名勒停，放歸田里。

translations.literal: An edict with Dun together removed their names and dismissed them, sending them back to their villages.
translations.idiomatic: He and Dun were struck from the rolls and sent home.

sentences.zh: 蔡京為相，復拜刑部、禮部侍郎，為翰林學士，進承旨。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing became chief minister he was again made Vice Minister of Justice and Rites and Hanlin Academician, advanced to Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing took power he returned as justice and rites vice minister, Hanlin academician, then expositor.

sentences.zh: 有言其在先帝遏密中以音樂自娛者，黜知汝州。

translations.literal: Some said that during the late emperor's period of restrained mourning he entertained himself with music; he was demoted to know Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of playing music during Shenzong's mourning, he was sent to Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年，徙蘇州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was moved to Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Su Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐縱部民盜鑄錢，謫單州團練副使、江州安置。

translations.literal: Because he indulged his subordinates in counterfeiting coin he was banished to Regiment Vice Commander of Dan Prefecture and settled at Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For allowing subordinates to counterfeit coin he was banished to Dan as regiment vice commander and settled at Jiang.

sentences.zh: 又坐守蘇時以天寧節同其父忌日，輒於前一日設宴，及節日不張樂，移永州。

translations.literal: Again because while guarding Su he held a banquet on the day before the Tianning Festival coincided with his father's death anniversary and on the festival day did not suspend music, he was moved to Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was also moved to Yong for holding a banquet the day before Tianning coincided with his father's death day and refusing to stop music on the festival.

sentences.zh: 會赦，復官中奉大夫，遂卒。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came he was restored to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and then died.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he was restored to grand master of palace attendance and died.

sentences.zh: 序辰亦有文，善傅會，深文刻覈，似其父云。

translations.literal: Xuchen also had literary talent, was skilled at attaching himself, applied the law in severe written detail—like his father.
translations.idiomatic: Xuchen too wrote well, excelled at flattery, and prosecuted harshly like his father.

sentences.zh: 徐鐸，字振文，興化莆田人。

translations.literal: Xu Duo, styled Zhenwen, was a native of Putian in Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Duo, who styled himself Zhenwen, came from Putian in Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 熙寧進士第一，簽書鎮東軍判官，紹聖末，以給事中直學士院。

translations.literal: He ranked first in the Xining jinshi, signed as secretary of the Zhendong Army judge, and at the end of Shaosheng was Gentlemen Attendant in the Direct Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the Xining jinshi, served as Zhendong Army signing secretary, and late in Shaosheng was gentlement attendant in the direct academy.

sentences.zh: 蹇序辰建議編類元祐諸臣章牘事狀，詔鐸同主之。

translations.literal: When Jian Xuchen proposed compiling Yuanyou ministers' memorials and case situations, an edict ordered Duo to direct it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian Xuchen proposed compiling Yuanyou files, Duo was ordered to co-direct the project.

sentences.zh: 凡一時施行文書，攈拾附著，纖悉不遺。

translations.literal: All documents then in force were gathered and attached—nothing minute was omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Every document then in force was gathered, omitting nothing.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 鐸雖云封駁，而是時凡給事中不肯書讀者，輒命代行之。

translations.literal: Though Duo was said to seal and rebut, at that time whenever a gentlement attendant refused to write approval he was ordered to act in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Though called a reviewing officer, whenever a gentlement attendant refused to sign, Duo was ordered to sign instead.

sentences.zh: 貢院獲舉人挾書，開封尹蔣之奇將以徒定罪，鐸爭不可，之奇為從輕比。

translations.literal: At the examination hall candidates with books were seized; Kaifeng Prefect Jiang Zhiqi was about to convict them as laborers; Duo contended it could not be done and Zhiqi followed a lighter statute.
translations.idiomatic: When examinees were caught with books, Kaifeng prefect Jiang Zhiqi wanted labor sentences; Duo protested and Jiang chose a lighter penalty.

sentences.zh: 既上省，章惇怒，罰府吏，舉人竟坐刑，鐸不復敢有言，眾傳以為笑。

translations.literal: After it reached the Secretariat Zhang Dun was angry, punished prefect clerks, and the candidates still sat for punishment; Duo no longer dared speak—crowds spread it as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun still punished clerks and candidates; Duo fell silent and became a public joke.

sentences.zh: 後議除御史中丞，或摭此事以為無所執持，乃止。

translations.literal: Later when discussing appointing him Censor-in-Chief, some seized this matter as showing no firm stand, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he was discussed for censor-in-chief, critics cited his silence and the appointment died.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，以龍圖閣待制知青州。

translations.literal: When the Huizong Emperor ascended the throne he was made Academician Awaiting Orders at the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huizong he became dragon-diagram academician and Qing prefect.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞豐稷論鐸編類事狀，率視章惇好惡為輕重，存歿名臣，橫罹竄斥，序辰既放歸田里，鐸之罪不在其下。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Feng Ji impeached Duo for compiling case situations, generally weighing light or heavy according to Zhang Dun's likes and dislikes, so that living and dead famous ministers were wrongly banished; since Xuchen was already sent to his village, Duo's crime was not below his.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Feng Ji charged that Duo had compiled cases to Zhang Dun's likes, exiling famous ministers living and dead; Xuchen had already been banished, but Duo's crime was no lesser.

sentences.zh: 詔落職知湖州。

translations.literal: An edict removed his post and made him know Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office and sent to Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era he was made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning he became minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 方議廟制，鐸請增為九室。

translations.literal: When temple regulation was debated, Duo asked to increase to nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: During temple debates he urged nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 議者疑已祧之主不可復祔、鐸言：「唐之獻祖、中宗、代宗與本朝之僖祖，皆嘗祧而復，今宜存宣祖於當祧，復翼祖於已祧，禮無不稱。」

translations.literal: Debaters doubted that already removed lords could be enshrined again; Duo said, "Tang's Xianzu, Zhongzong, and Daizong and this dynasty's Xizu all were once removed and restored; now it is fitting to keep Xuanzu in the place of removal and restore Yizu in the place already removed—ritual permits no objection."
translations.idiomatic: Critics doubted re-enthroning removed ancestors; Duo cited Tang and Song precedents for restoring removed spirits and restoring Yizu while keeping Xuanzu in place.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 進吏部尚書，卒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Personnel and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of personnel and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：士學不為己，而俯仰隨時，如挈皋居井上，求其立朝不撓，不可得已。

translations.literal: The critique says: When scholars' learning is not for themselves but they bow and rise with the times, like Qie Gao dwelling above a well, to seek that they stand at court unbending is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The historians remark that scholars who do not study for themselves but sway with the times cannot be expected to stand upright at court.

sentences.zh: 常秩在嘉祐、治平時，三辭羔雁之聘，若能隱居以求其志者；

translations.literal: Chang Zhi in the Jiayou and Zhiping eras thrice declined lamb-and-wild-goose appointments—if one could hide and seek his aim;
translations.idiomatic: Chang Zhi thrice declined court summons in Jiayou and Zhiping as if he sought to live by principle;

sentences.zh: 及王安石用事，一召即至，容容歷年，曾無一嘉謨，而竊顯位。

translations.literal: when Wang Anshi held power, at one summons he came, went along compliantly for years, yet never had one good counsel while stealing a prominent post.
translations.idiomatic: yet when Wang Anshi took power one summons brought him, and for years he offered no worthy counsel while keeping high office.

sentences.zh: 至定之黨附，亶之凶德，宜為世所指名。

translations.literal: As for Ding's faction attachment and Dan's vicious conduct—they should be named by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ding's factionalism and Shu Dan's viciousness deserve the age's condemnation.

sentences.zh: 綰及周輔二家，父子並同惡相濟，而序辰與鐸編類事狀，流毒元祐名臣，忠義之士，為之一空，馴致靖康之禍，可勝歎哉。

translations.literal: Wan's and Zhoufu's two families—father and son together aiding evil; while Xuchen and Duo compiled case situations, poisoning Yuanyou famous ministers until loyal and righteous men were emptied, gently leading to the Jingkang calamity—how much can one sigh!
translations.idiomatic: The Deng and Jian clans fathered and sonned evil together; Xuchen and Duo compiled blacklist files that poisoned Yuanyou worthies, emptied loyal men, and helped bring the Jingkang disaster—lamentable indeed.

sentences.zh: 王廣淵

translations.literal: Wang Guangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangyuan.

sentences.zh: 王廣淵，字才叔，大名成安人。

translations.literal: Wang Guangyuan, styled Caishu, was a native of Cheng'an in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangyuan, who styled himself Caishu, came from Cheng'an in Daming.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，上曾祖《明家集》，詔官其後，廣淵推與弟廣廉，而以進士為大理法直官、編排中書文字。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era he presented his great-grandfather's "Collection for an Enlightened House"; an edict gave office to his descendants—Guangyuan yielded to his younger brother Guanglian and with the jinshi degree was made Law Officer of the Court of Judicial Review and Compiler of Zhongshu Texts.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli he presented his great-grandfather's Collection for an Enlightened House; the throne offered office to descendants, but Guangyuan yielded to his brother Guanglian and took the jinshi path as a judicial-review law officer and Zhongshu compiler.

sentences.zh: 裁定祖宗御書千卷，仁宗喜之，以知舒州，留不行。

translations.literal: He collated a thousand scrolls of ancestral imperial writings; Renzong was pleased and made him know Shu Prefecture but he stayed and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He collated a thousand scrolls of imperial writings; Renzong pleased, offered him Shu Prefecture, but he stayed at court.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，言者劾其漏泄禁中語，出知齊州，改京東轉運使，得於內省傳達章奏。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor ascended the throne, remonstrators impeached him for leaking forbidden-palace words; he was sent out to know Qi Prefecture, changed to Huaidong transport commissioner, and was allowed to relay memorials inside the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong's accession brought impeachment for leaking palace secrets; he went to Qi Prefecture, became Huaidong transport commissioner, and was allowed to relay memorials inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 曾公亮、王安石持不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang and Wang Anshi held it impossible and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang and Wang Anshi blocked the privilege and it ended.

sentences.zh: 廣淵以方春農事興而民苦乏，兼並之家得以乘急要利，乞留本道錢帛五十萬，貸之貧民，歲可獲息二十五萬，從之。

translations.literal: Guangyuan said that in early spring farming was rising while the people suffered want, and consolidating households could seize urgency for profit; he begged to retain five hundred thousand of the circuit's cash and silk to lend to poor people, yearly gaining interest of two hundred fifty thousand—approved.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that spring farming began while the poor lacked cash, letting rich lenders profit; he asked to keep five hundred thousand strings to lend at interest of two hundred fifty thousand a year, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 其事與青苗錢法合，安石始以為可用，召至京師。

translations.literal: The matter matched the Green Sprouts money law; Anshi at first thought him usable and summoned him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The plan matched Green Sprouts lending; Anshi first thought him useful and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞呂公著摭其舊惡，還故官。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Lü Gongzhu seized his old crimes and he returned to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Lü Gongzhu cited old crimes and he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 程顥、李常又論其抑配掊克，迎朝廷旨意以困百姓。

translations.literal: Cheng Hao and Li Chang again argued he forced allotments and extorted, welcoming court intent to distress the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hao and Li Chang accused him of forced allotments and extortion to please the court and harm the people.

sentences.zh: 會河北轉運使劉庠不散青苗錢奏適至，安石曰：「廣淵力主新法而遭劾，劉庠故壞新法而不問，舉事如此，安得人無向背？」

translations.literal: Just then Hebei transport commissioner Liu Xiang's memorial refusing to distribute Green Sprouts money arrived; Anshi said, "Guangyuan strongly upholds the new laws yet suffers impeachment; Liu Xiang deliberately harms the new laws yet is not questioned—conduct affairs thus, how can people lack taking sides?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xiang refused to distribute Green Sprouts funds in Hebei, Anshi asked why Guangyuan was impeached for supporting reforms while Liu Xiang was not punished for opposing them.

sentences.zh: 故顥與常言不行。

translations.literal: Therefore Hao's and Chang's words were not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and Chang were ignored.

sentences.zh: 徙使河東，擢寶文閣待制、知慶州。

translations.literal: He was moved to commissioner of Hedong and promoted to Academician Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Treasured Writings and prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hedong commissioner, then treasured-writings academician and Qing prefect.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使興師入夏境，檄慶會兵。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner raised troops and entered Xia territory; he ordered Qing to assemble troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the pacification commissioner invaded Xia, Guangyuan was ordered to mobilize Qing troops.

sentences.zh: 方授甲，卒長吳逵以眾亂，廣淵亟召五營兵禦之。

translations.literal: Just as armor was issued, company leader Wu Kui mutinied with the troops; Guangyuan urgently summoned five-camp soldiers to defend.
translations.idiomatic: As armor was issued, company leader Wu Kui mutinied; Guangyuan summoned five camps to defend.

sentences.zh: 逵率二千人斬關出，廣淵遣部將姚兕、林廣追擊，降其眾。

translations.literal: Kui led two thousand men to cut through the gate and exit; Guangyuan sent subordinate generals Yao Si and Lin Guang in pursuit and accepted the surrender of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Kui broke out with two thousand men; Guangyuan sent Yao Si and Lin Guang to pursue and accept surrender.

sentences.zh: 柔遠三都戍卒欲應賊，不果，廣淵陽勞之，使還戍，潛遣兵間道邀襲，盡戮之。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers of the three Rouyuan commands wished to join the rebels but did not succeed; Guangyuan feigned to comfort them and sent them back to garrison, secretly sending troops by a bypath to intercept and strike, slaughtering them all.
translations.idiomatic: Rouyuan garrison troops nearly joined the mutiny; Guangyuan feigned kindness, sent them back, then ambushed and slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 猶以盜發所部，削兩秩。

translations.literal: He was still punished with two ranks stripped because banditry broke out in his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: He still lost two ranks because rebellion erupted in his district.

sentences.zh: 二年，進龍圖閣直學士、知渭州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced to Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made to know Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became direct dragon-diagram academician and Wei prefect.

sentences.zh: 廣淵小有才而善附會，所辟置類非其人。

translations.literal: Guangyuan had small talent but was skilled at attaching himself; those he appointed were mostly not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan had modest talent but excelled at flattery and appointed unfit men.

sentences.zh: 帝謂執政曰：「廣淵奏辟將佐，非貴遊子弟，即胥史輩，至於濮宮書吏亦預選，蓋其人與時君卿善。

translations.literal: The emperor told the administrators: "Guangyuan memorialized appointing aides and assistants—not sons of noble houses but clerk sorts, even clerks of the Pu Palace were in the selection, probably because the men were friendly with Shijunqing of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told ministers that Guangyuan's appointments were not noble sons but clerks, even Pu Palace scribes, likely because they were friends of powerful patrons.

sentences.zh: 一路官吏不少，置而不取，乃用此輩，豈不誤朝廷事？

translations.literal: There are no few officials in a circuit, yet he set them aside and used this crowd—does he not mistake court affairs?
translations.idiomatic: He ignored many qualified circuit officials for such men—was that not a court mistake?

sentences.zh: 已下詔切責，卿等宜貽書申戒之。」

translations.literal: An edict has already sternly rebuked him; you should send letters to warn him."
translations.idiomatic: An edict had already rebuked him; ministers should write further warnings.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十，贈右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He died at sixty and was posthumously given Right Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty and was posthumously honored as Right Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，詔以其被遇先帝之故，弟臨自皇城使擢為兵部郎中、直昭文館，子得君賜進士出身。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng an edict because he had received favor from the late emperor made his younger brother Lin from Imperial City Commissioner advanced to Bureau Director in the Ministry of War and Direct Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and his son Dejun granted jinshi status.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng, because Guangyuan had enjoyed Shenzong's favor, his brother Lin rose from imperial-city commissioner to war bureau director and Zhaowen academician, and his son Dejun received jinshi status.

sentences.zh: 弟 臨

translations.literal: Younger brother: Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Lin.

sentences.zh: 臨，字大觀，亦起進士，簽書雄州判官。

translations.literal: Lin, styled Daguan, also rose through the jinshi, signed as secretary of the Xiong Prefecture judge.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, who styled himself Daguan, also earned the jinshi and served as Xiong signing secretary.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐初，契丹泛使至，朝論疑所應，臨言：「契丹方饑困，何能為？

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiayou Khitan envoys on general mission arrived; court debate doubted how to respond; Lin said, "The Khitan are now hungry and distressed—what can they do?
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiayou, when Khitan envoys arrived, Lin argued they were too hungry and weak to threaten Song.

sentences.zh: 然《春秋》許與之義，不可以不謹。

translations.literal: Yet the Spring and Autumn's principle of granting requests cannot but be careful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Spring and Autumn principle of granting requests still required caution.

sentences.zh: 彼嘗求馴象，可拒而不拒；

translations.literal: They once sought tame elephants—could refuse yet did not refuse;
translations.idiomatic: They had once sought tame elephants and Song could have refused but did not;

sentences.zh: 嘗求樂章，可與而不與，兩失之矣。

translations.literal: once sought music chapters—could grant yet did not grant—both were losses.
translations.idiomatic: they had sought music texts and Song could have granted them but did not—both were mistakes.

sentences.zh: 今橫使之來，或謂其求聖像，聖像果可與哉？」

translations.literal: Now the envoy on horizontal mission comes; some say he seeks a sage image—can a sage image truly be granted?"
translations.idiomatic: Now this envoy perhaps sought a sage image—which could not be granted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷善其議。

translations.literal: The court approved his argument.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his argument.

sentences.zh: 治平中，詔求武略，用近臣薦，自屯田員外郎換崇儀使、知順安軍，改河北沿邊安撫都監。

translations.literal: During Zhiping an edict sought military talent; on recommendation of a near minister he was changed from Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue to Commissioner of Honored Rites and made to know the Shun'an Army, then changed to Metropolitan Frontier Pacification Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiping, recommended for military talent, he left the revenue vice directorship for honored-rites commissioner and Shun'an command, then Hebei frontier pacification.

sentences.zh: 上備禦數十策，大略皆自治而已。

translations.literal: He submitted several tens of strategies for defense—mostly self-governance.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted dozens of defense plans focused chiefly on strengthening Song itself.

sentences.zh: 契丹刺兩輸人為義軍，來歸者數萬。

translations.literal: The Khitan drove people of the two Shus as righteous armies; those who came to submit numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan raids drove tens of thousands of Shus people to defect to Song.

sentences.zh: 或請遣還，臨曰：「彼歸我而遣之，必為亂，不如因而撫之。」

translations.literal: Some asked to send them back; Lin said, "If they return to us and we send them back, they will surely rebel—better to comfort them thereby."
translations.idiomatic: Some wanted to return them; Lin said repatriation would breed rebellion, so they should be settled instead.

sentences.zh: 詔從其請，自是來者益多，契丹悔失計。

translations.literal: An edict followed his request; from this those who came grew more numerous and the Khitan regretted their miscalculation.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed; more defectors followed and the Khitan regretted the policy.

sentences.zh: 進安撫副使，歷知涇、鄜州、廣信、安肅軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Pacification Commissioner and successively knew Jing, Zou prefectures, Guangxin, and the Ansu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice pacification commissioner and governed Jing, Zou, Guangxin, and Ansu.

sentences.zh: 召對，還文階，知齊州、滄州、荊南，入為戶部副使，以寶文閣待制知廣州府、河中，卒。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he returned to civil rank, knew Qi, Cang, and Jingnan, entered as Vice Minister of Revenue, and with Academician Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Treasured Writings knew Guangzhou Prefecture and Hezhong, then died.
translations.idiomatic: After an audience he returned to civil rank, governed Qi, Cang, and Jingnan, became vice minister of revenue, then treasured-writings academician in Guangzhou and Hezhong, and died.

sentences.zh: 王陶，字樂道，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wang Tao, styled Ledao, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tao, who styled himself Ledao, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 第進士，至太常丞而丁父憂。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and reached Grand Master of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices when his father died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and was grand master of imperial sacrifices when his father died.

sentences.zh: 陶以登朝在郊祀後，恩不及親，乞還所遷官，丐追贈。

translations.literal: Tao, because he had entered court after the suburban sacrifice, his favor did not reach his parent; he begged to return offices he had advanced and asked posthumous enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had entered court after the suburban sacrifice, his father missed the favor; Tao asked to return his promotions and secure posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 詔特聽之，仍俟服闋，除太子中允。

translations.literal: An edict specially permitted it and still waited until mourning ended to appoint him Crown Prince Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The court specially allowed it and appointed him crown prince attendant after mourning.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐初，為監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiayou he was made Acting Supervising Censor in the Inner Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiayou he became acting supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 衛卒入延福宮為盜，有司引疏決恩降其罪。

translations.literal: Guards entered Yanfu Palace as thieves; the responsible office cited commutation and grace to reduce their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Guards robbed Yanfu Palace; officials sought commuted sentences.

sentences.zh: 陶曰：「禁省之嚴，不應用外間會降為比。」

translations.literal: Tao said, "The forbidden precinct's severity should not use outer-court amnesty reductions as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Tao said palace crimes should not be reduced by outer-court amnesty precedents.

sentences.zh: 於是流諸海島，主者皆論罰。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were exiled to the sea islands and the responsible officials were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: They were exiled to the islands and responsible officials were punished.

sentences.zh: 中貴人導煉丹者入禁廷，陶言：「漢、唐方士，名為化黃金、益年壽以惑人主者，後皆就戮。

translations.literal: A palace favorite guided an alchemist into the forbidden court; Tao said, "Han and Tang alchemists, named as turning yellow gold and extending years to delude rulers, were later all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch brought an alchemist into the palace, Tao cited Han and Tang rulers who executed such men.

sentences.zh: 請出之。」

translations.literal: I pray he be removed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the man be expelled.

sentences.zh: 陳升之為樞密副使，論其不當，升之去，陶亦知衛州，改蔡州。

translations.literal: Chen Shengzhi was Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and argued it was improper; when Shengzhi left, Tao also knew Weizhou and was changed to Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengzhi opposed the move; when Chen left, Tao was sent to Weizhou, then Cai.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以右正言召。

translations.literal: The next year he was again summoned as Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled as right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 陶言：「臣與四人同補郡，今獨兩人召，請並還唐介、呂誨等。」

translations.literal: Tao said, "I with four men together were given prefectures; now only two are summoned—I pray Tang Jie and Lü Hui also be returned."
translations.idiomatic: Tao asked that Tang Jie and Lü Hui be recalled with him since four men had been sent to prefectures but only two were summoned back.

sentences.zh: 英宗知宗正寺，逾年不就職。

translations.literal: The Yingzong Emperor knew the Directorate of the Imperial Clan but for more than a year did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong headed the imperial clan directorate but delayed taking office for over a year.

sentences.zh: 陶上疏曰：「自至和中聖躬違豫之後，天下顒顒，無所寄命，交章抗疏，請早擇宗室親賢，以建儲嗣，危言切語，動天感人。

translations.literal: Tao submitted: "Since in the Zhihe era the sage person was unwell, the realm has looked up with nowhere to entrust its mandate; memorials and remonstrances piled up, begging early selection of a worthy imperial clansman to establish the heir—severe words and cutting phrases moved Heaven and touched men.
translations.idiomatic: Tao memorialized that since Yingzong's illness in Zhihe the realm had lacked a clear heir and memorials had begged for a worthy imperial clansman as successor.

sentences.zh: 夫為是議者，豈皆懷不忠孝、為奸利附託之人哉？

translations.literal: Were those who made such proposals all men harboring disloyalty and unfilial piety, doing wicked profit and clinging attachment?
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether such advocates were all disloyal schemers.

sentences.zh: 發於至誠，念宗廟社稷無窮大計而已。

translations.literal: They sprang from utmost sincerity, thinking only of the endless great plan of the ancestral temple and altars.
translations.idiomatic: He answered that they acted from sincerity for the state's long-term good.

sentences.zh: 陛下順民欲而安人心，故親發德音，銳為此舉，中外搖搖之心，一旦定矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty followed the people's desire and settled people's hearts, so personally issuing a virtuous pronouncement you sharply undertook this measure—the hearts of inside and outside that swayed were settled in a day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had followed public will to settle hearts by announcing succession plans.

sentences.zh: 厥後浸潤稽緩，豈免憂疑？

translations.literal: Afterward gradual delay—how could worry and doubt be avoided?
translations.idiomatic: Later delays revived public anxiety.

sentences.zh: 流言或云事由嬪御、宦侍姑息之語，聖意因而惑焉。

translations.literal: Rumors said the matter came from palace women and eunuchs' indulgent words, and the sage mind was thereby confused.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors blamed palace women and eunuchs for confusing the emperor.

sentences.zh: 婦人近幸，詎識遠圖？

translations.literal: Women and near favorites—how can they know far-reaching plans?
translations.idiomatic: Tao asked how women and favorites could grasp statecraft.

sentences.zh: 臣恐海內民庶，謂陛下始者順天意民心命之，今者聽左右姑息之言而疑之，使遠近奸邪得以窺間伺隙，可不惜哉！」

translations.literal: I fear the realm's people will say Your Majesty at first followed Heaven's intent and the people's hearts in ordering it, but now listens to the indulgent words of those at your side and doubts it, letting distant and near treachery spy gaps—can this not be cherished!"
translations.idiomatic: He warned that the public might think the emperor first followed Heaven and the people, then listened to indulgent courtiers and invited treachery.

sentences.zh: 因請對，仁宗曰：「今當別與一名目。」

translations.literal: He therefore asked for an audience; Renzong said, "Now another title should be given."
translations.idiomatic: He sought audience; Renzong said another title would be used.

sentences.zh: 既而韓琦決策，遂立為皇子。

translations.literal: Soon Han Qi decided the policy and he was established as imperial son.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi soon secured his establishment as imperial son.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，加直史館、修起居注、皇子位伴讀、淮陽潁王府詡善、知制誥，進龍圖閣學士、知永興軍，召為太子詹事。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor ascended the throne he was given Direct Historiographer, Concurrent Compiler of the Imperial Diary, Companion Reader to the Heir's Position, Instructor of the Huaiyang and Ying Princes' Establishments, Drafting Official, advanced to Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Yongxing Army, summoned as Crown Prince Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong succeeded, Tao became direct historiographer, imperial diary compiler, heir's tutor, drafting official, dragon-diagram academician, Yongxing prefect, then crown prince tutor.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，遷樞密直學士，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor ascended the throne he was moved to Academician Direct of the Bureau of Military Affairs and made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong he became bureau of military affairs academician direct and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 郭逵以簽書樞密宣撫陝西，詔令還都。

translations.literal: Guo Kui as Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi—an edict ordered him to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Kui, signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Shaanxi pacification commissioner, was ordered back to court.

sentences.zh: 陶言：「韓琦置逵二府，至用太祖故事，出師劫制人主，琦必有奸言惑亂聖德。

translations.literal: Tao said, "Han Qi placed Kui in two offices, even using Taizu precedent, going out as commander to coerce the ruler—Qi must have treacherous words confusing the sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Tao charged that Han Qi had used Taizu precedent to let Guo Kui coerce the throne with military power.

sentences.zh: 願罷逵為渭州。」

translations.literal: I pray Kui be dismissed to Wei Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Guo Kui be demoted to Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「逵先帝所用，今無罪黜之，是章先帝用人之失也，不可。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Kui was used by the late emperor; now to dismiss him without crime is to display the late emperor's error in using men—impossible."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, saying dismissing Shenzong's appointee would expose the late emperor's error.

sentences.zh: 陶既不得逞，遂以琦不押文德常朝班奏劾之。

translations.literal: Tao, unable to prevail, then impeached Qi for not stamping the Wende regular court roster.
translations.idiomatic: Foiled, Tao impeached Qi for failing to stamp the Wende court roster.

sentences.zh: 陶始受知於琦，驟加獎拔。

translations.literal: Tao at first received recognition from Qi and was suddenly praised and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Tao had once owed his rise to Qi's patronage.

sentences.zh: 帝初臨御，頗不悅執政之專，陶料必易置大臣，欲自規重位，故視琦如仇，力攻之，琦閉門待罪。

translations.literal: The emperor at first taking the throne was quite displeased with the administrators' monopoly; Tao calculated that great ministers would surely be replaced and wished to scheme for a heavy post himself, so he viewed Qi as an enemy and attacked forcefully; Qi closed his door awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong disliked dominating ministers; Tao hoped to seize high office and attacked Qi like an enemy while Qi awaited punishment behind closed doors.

sentences.zh: 帝徙陶為翰林學士，旋出知陳州，入權三司使。

translations.literal: The emperor moved Tao to Hanlin Academician, soon sent out to know Chen Prefecture, entered to act as Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him Hanlin academician, then Chen prefect, then acting Three Departments commissioner.

sentences.zh: 呂公著言其反覆不可近，又以侍讀學士知蔡州，歷河南府、許、汝、陳三州，以東宮舊臣加觀文殿學士。

translations.literal: Lü Gongzhu said his reversals made him unapproachable; again as Lecturer Academician he knew Cai Prefecture, passed through Henan Prefecture and Xu, Ru, and Chen, and as an old Eastern Palace minister was given Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gongzhu called him untrustworthy; he governed Cai, Henan, Xu, Ru, and Chen and received viewing-literature academician as an old palace tutor.

sentences.zh: 帝終薄其為人，不復用。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end despised his person and did not reuse him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately despised him and never reused him.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，卒，年六十一，贈吏部尚書，諡曰「文恪」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng he died at sixty-one; he was posthumously given Minister of Personnel and the posthumous title "Wénkè."
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanfeng's third year at sixty-one, posthumously honored as personnel minister with the temple name Wenke.

sentences.zh: 陶微時苦貧，寓京師教小學。

translations.literal: When Tao was young he suffered poverty and lodged in the capital teaching elementary school.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Tao was poor and taught elementary school in the capital.

sentences.zh: 其友姜愚氣豪樂施，一日大雪，念陶奉母寒餒，荷一鍤剗雪，行二十里訪之。

translations.literal: His friend Jiang Yu was bold and generous; one day in great snow, thinking of Tao's mother cold and hungry, he shouldered a spade and cut through snow, walking twenty li to visit.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Jiang Yu, generous and bold, once shoveled through snow for twenty li to visit Tao in poverty.

sentences.zh: 陶母子凍坐，日高無炊煙。

translations.literal: Tao and his mother sat frozen; the sun was high with no cooking smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Tao and his mother sat freezing with no fire by midday.

sentences.zh: 愚亟出解所衣錦裘，質錢買酒肉、薪炭，與附火飲食，又捐數百千為之娶。

translations.literal: Yu hastily took off his brocade fur coat, pawned it to buy wine, meat, fuel, and charcoal, and fed them by the fire; he also gave several hundred strings to marry Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu pawned his fur coat for food and fuel, warmed them, and gave hundreds of strings for Tao's marriage.

sentences.zh: 陶既貴，尹洛，愚老而喪明，自衛州新鄉往謁之，意陶必念舊哀己。

translations.literal: After Tao was honored he governed Luoyang; Yu was old and blind and came from Xinxiang in Weizhou to visit him, thinking Tao would surely remember old kindness to himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao governed Luoyang, blind old Yu came from Xinxiang expecting gratitude.

sentences.zh: 陶對之邈然，但出尊酒而已。

translations.literal: Tao received him distantly and only offered fine wine.
translations.idiomatic: Tao received him coldly and offered only wine.

sentences.zh: 愚大失望，歸而病死。

translations.literal: Yu was greatly disappointed, returned, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yu went home disappointed and died.

sentences.zh: 聞者益薄陶之為人。

translations.literal: Those who heard it further despised Tao's person.
translations.idiomatic: Observers despised Tao even more.

sentences.zh: 王子韶

translations.literal: Wang Zishao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zishao.

sentences.zh: 王子韶，字聖美，太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Zishao, styled Shengmei, was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zishao, who styled himself Shengmei, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，以年未冠守選，復遊太學，久之乃得調。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; because he had not yet reached the cap he guarded selection, again wandered the Grand Academy, and only after long time obtained an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi but, still under age, waited for appointment, studied longer at the academy, and only later received a post.

sentences.zh: 王安石引入條例司，擢監察御史裏行，出按明州苗振獄。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi brought him into the Regulations Office and promoted him to Supervising Censor in the Inner Bureau, sent out to investigate Miao Zhen's case in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi brought him into the Regulations Office, made him acting supervising censor, and sent him to investigate Miao Zhen in Ming.

sentences.zh: 安石惡祖無擇，子韶迎其意，發無擇在杭州時事，自京師逮對，而以振獄付張載，無擇遂廢。

translations.literal: Anshi hated Zu Wuzi; Zishao catered to his intent, exposing Wuzi's affairs when in Hang Prefecture, summoned from the capital for audience, while handing the Zhen case to Zhang Zai—Wuzi was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi hated Zu Wuzi; Zishao exposed Wuzi's Hangzhou conduct, had him summoned to court, and handed the Zhen case to Zhang Zai until Wuzi fell.

sentences.zh: 中丞呂公著等論新法，一臺盡罷。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Lü Gongzhu and others debated the new laws—the whole bureau was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Gongzhu and other censors debated the new laws, the whole bureau was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 子韶出知上元縣，遷湖南轉運判官。

translations.literal: Zishao was sent out to know Shangyuan County, moved to Vice Transport Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zishao became Shangyuan magistrate, then Hunan vice transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 御史張商英劾其不葬父母，貶知高郵縣。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Shangying impeached him for not burying his parents and he was demoted to know Gaoyou County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shangying impeached him for failing to bury his parents and he was demoted to Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 由司農丞提舉兩浙常平。

translations.literal: From Ministry of Revenue aide he was put in charge of the two Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: From revenue aide he took charge of the two Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 入對，神宗與論字學，留為資善堂修定《說文》官。

translations.literal: Entering for audience, the Shenzong Emperor discussed philology with him and retained him as officer revising the "Shuowen" at the Hall of Cultivated Virtues.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Shenzong discussed philology with him and kept him to revise the Shuowen at the Hall of Cultivated Virtues.

sentences.zh: 官制行，為禮部員外郎，以入省後期，改庫部。

translations.literal: When the office system was enacted he was Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites; because he was late entering the Secretariat he was changed to the Storehouse Department.
translations.idiomatic: Under the new offices he was rites vice director, then moved to the storehouse department for late entry.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，歷吏部郎中、衛尉少卿，遷太常諫官。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he passed through Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Guards, moved to Remonstrance Official of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou he served as personnel bureau director and guards vice director, then imperial-sacrifices remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 劉安世言：「熙寧初，士大夫有『十鑽』之目，子韶為『衙內鑽』，指其交結要人子弟，如刀鑽之利。

translations.literal: Liu Anshi said: "In early Xining among scholar-officials there was the 'ten augers' list; Zishao was the 'yamen auger,' pointing to his connecting with powerful men's sons like an auger's profit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anshi said early Xining officials listed ten augers, calling Zishao the yamen auger for courting powerful men's sons.

sentences.zh: 又陷祖無擇於深文，搢紳所共鄙薄，豈宜汙禮樂之地！」

translations.literal: He also trapped Zu Wuzi in severe law—gentry together despise him; how can he stain the place of rites and music!
translations.idiomatic: He also trapped Zu Wuzi with harsh law; how could such a man hold a ritual post?

sentences.zh: 改衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to director of the court of imperial guards.

sentences.zh: 安世復言：「七寺正卿班少常上，因彈擊而獲超遷，是啟僥幸也。」

translations.literal: Anshi again said: "The seven directorates' chief ministers rank above the vice director of imperial sacrifices; because of impeachment he obtained leap promotion—this opens opportunism."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi protested that leap promotion after impeachment encouraged opportunism.

sentences.zh: 乃出知滄州。

translations.literal: He was then sent out to know Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為秘書少監，迎伴遼使，御下苛刻，軍吏因被酒刃傷子韶及其子。

translations.literal: He entered as Vice Director of the Secretariat, received Khitan envoys, treated subordinates harshly, and army clerks wounded Zishao and his son while drunk.
translations.idiomatic: As secretariat vice director escorting Khitan envoys, he treated subordinates harshly and drunken clerks wounded him and his son.

sentences.zh: 又出知濟州，建言乞追復先烈以貽後法，復以太常少卿召，進秘書監，拜集賢殿修撰、知明州，卒。

translations.literal: Again sent out to know Ji Prefecture; he submitted asking to restore the former emperors to leave later law, again summoned as Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices, advanced to Director of the Secretariat, made Compiler at the Hall of Cultivated Talents and prefect of Ming, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Ji, he urged restoring former emperors' rites, returned as imperial-sacrifices vice director, rose to secretariat director and cultivated-talents compiler in Ming, and died.

sentences.zh: 崇寧二年，子相錄元祐中所上疏稿聞於朝，詔贈顯謨閣待制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongning his son Xiang recorded Yuanyou memorials and the court learned of them; an edict posthumously gave Displayed Counsel Academician Awaiting Orders.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning's second year his son Xiang published Yuanyou memorials; the court posthumously made him displayed-counsel academician.

sentences.zh: 何正臣

translations.literal: He Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhengchen.

sentences.zh: 何正臣，字君表，臨江新淦人。

translations.literal: He Zhengchen, styled Junbiao, was a native of Xingan in Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhengchen, who styled himself Junbiao, came from Xingan in Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 九歲舉童子，賜出身，復中進士第。

translations.literal: At nine he passed the child prodigy examination and was granted status; he again passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he passed the child prodigy exam and later the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，用蔡確薦，為御史裏行。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng era, on Cai Que's recommendation, he was made Acting Censor in the Inner Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng, on Cai Que's recommendation, he became acting censor.

sentences.zh: 遂與李定、舒亶論蘇軾，得五品服，領三班院。

translations.literal: He then with Li Ding and Shu Dan impeached Su Shi, obtained fifth-rank dress, and headed the Third Class Court.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Ding and Shu Dan he impeached Su Shi, gained fifth-rank dress, and headed the Third Class Court.

sentences.zh: 會正御史專六察，正臣言：「幸得備言路，以激濁揚清為職，不宜兼治它曹。」

translations.literal: Just then regular censors specialized in six inspections; Zhengchen said, "Fortunately I can fill the remonstrance path, taking stirring the muddy and raising the clear as duty—I should not concurrently administer other bureaus."
translations.idiomatic: When censors specialized in six inspections, Zhengchen said remonstrance duty should not be mixed with other bureaus.

sentences.zh: 神宗善之，為悉罷御史兼局，而正臣解三班，加直集賢院，擢侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: The Shenzong Emperor approved it, entirely abolished censors' concurrent bureaus, while Zhengchen left the Third Class Court, was given Direct Jixian Hall, and promoted to Supervising Censor with Concurrent Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong agreed, ended censor concurrent posts, made Zhengchen direct Jixian academician, and supervising censor with concurrent affairs.

sentences.zh: 韓存寶討瀘夷無功，命治其獄，被以逗撓罪誅之。

translations.literal: Han Cunbao campaigned against Lu barbarians without achievement; he was ordered to try the case and was charged with delay and cowardice and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to try Han Cunbao's failed Lu campaign, he had Han executed for delay and cowardice.

sentences.zh: 還，除寶文閣待制、知審官東院，尚書省建為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: On return he was made Academician Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Treasured Writings and to know the Eastern Court of Personnel Review; the Secretariat was built as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as treasured-writings academician and eastern personnel-review director, then personnel vice minister.

sentences.zh: 逾年，嫚於奉職，銓擬多牴牾。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was negligent in duty; appointments mostly conflicted.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he grew negligent and appointments often conflicted.

sentences.zh: 事聞，以制法未善為解。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he explained that the law was not yet good.
translations.idiomatic: When reported, he blamed the law rather than himself.

sentences.zh: 王安禮曰：「法未善，有司所當請，豈得歸罪於法？」

translations.literal: Wang Anli said, "If the law is not good, the office should request change—how can blame be laid on the law?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anli said bad law should be amended by officials, not blamed on the statute.

sentences.zh: 乃出知潭州。

translations.literal: He was then sent out to know Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Tan prefect.

sentences.zh: 時詔州縣聽民以家貲易鹽，吏或推行失指。

translations.literal: At that time an edict allowed prefectures and counties to let the people trade salt with family property; officials sometimes implemented it wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then let counties let people trade salt with family property, but officials often mishandled enforcement.

sentences.zh: 正臣條上其害，謂無益於民，亦不足以佐國用，遂寢之，民以為便。

translations.literal: Zhengchen itemized its harms, saying it did not benefit the people and was also insufficient to assist state revenue, so it was suspended and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchen listed its harms, saying it helped neither people nor revenue; the policy was suspended and people were relieved.

sentences.zh: 後歷刑部侍郎、知宣州，卒。

translations.literal: Later he passed through Vice Minister of Justice and knew Xuan Prefecture, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as justice vice minister and Xuan prefect, then died.

sentences.zh: 陳繹，字和叔，開封人。

translations.literal: Chen Yi, styled Heshu, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi, who styled himself Heshu, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，為館閣校勘、集賢校理，刊定《前漢書》，居母喪，詔即家讎校。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was made Collator of the Academy and Collation Scholar of the Jixian Hall, collated the "Former Han History," and when his mother died an edict ordered proofreading at home.
translations.idiomatic: After the jinshi he collated at the academy and Jixian Hall, worked on the Former Han History, and was ordered to proofread at home during mourning.

sentences.zh: 英宗臨政淵嘿，繹獻五箴，曰主斷、明微、廣度、省變、稽古。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor took power he was deep and silent; Yi presented five admonitions: decisive rule, clarifying subtleties, broad tolerance, reducing change, and examining antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When taciturn Yingzong took power, Yi offered five admonitions: decisive rule, clarity, breadth, restraint in change, and learning from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 同判刑部，獄訟有情法相忤者，讞之。

translations.literal: As Concurrent Judge of the Ministry of Justice, in lawsuits where sentiment and law conflicted he judged them.
translations.idiomatic: As concurrent justice judge he resolved cases where sentiment and law clashed.

sentences.zh: 或言刑曹唯知正是否，不當有所輕重。

translations.literal: Some said the penal office should only know correcting yes and no and should not have light or heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Some said the penal office should only judge right and wrong, not weigh severity.

sentences.zh: 繹曰：「持法者貴審允，心知失刑，惡得坐視？」

translations.literal: Yi said, "Those who hold the law value careful fairness; knowing in the heart that punishment is wrong, how can one sit and watch?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said law officers must be fair; knowing a sentence was wrong, how could one stand by?

sentences.zh: 由是多所平反。

translations.literal: From this many cases were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Many convictions were overturned.

sentences.zh: 帝稱其文學，以為實錄檢討官。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his literary learning and made him Compiler of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his scholarship and made him veritable-records compiler.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，為陝西轉運副使，入直舍人院、修起居注、知制誥，拜翰林學士，以侍講學士知鄧州。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor ascended the throne he was made Vice Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi, entered the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, compiled the imperial diary, was drafting official, made Hanlin Academician, and with Lecturer Academician knew Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong he became Shaanxi vice transport commissioner, academy custodian, diary compiler, drafting official, Hanlin academician, and Deng prefect with lecturer title.

sentences.zh: 繹不能肅閨門，子與婦一夕俱殞於卒伍之手，傲然無慚色。

translations.literal: Yi could not discipline his household; son and daughter-in-law in one night both perished at the hands of soldiers, yet he was proudly without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yi could not govern his household; his son and daughter-in-law were killed by soldiers in one night, yet he showed no shame.

sentences.zh: 召知通進銀臺司，帝語輔臣曰：「繹論事不避權貴。」

translations.literal: Summoned to know the Bureau for Transmission of Silver Terrace; the emperor told assisting ministers: "Yi discusses affairs without avoiding the powerful."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to head the Silver Terrace transmission bureau, the emperor told ministers Yi did not fear the powerful in debate.

sentences.zh: 命權開封府。

translations.literal: He was ordered to act as Kaifeng Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to act as Kaifeng prefect.

sentences.zh: 時獄有小疑，輒從中覆；

translations.literal: At that time in prison if there was small doubt it was always reviewed from the center;
translations.idiomatic: Small doubts in Kaifeng cases were usually reviewed centrally;

sentences.zh: 至繹，特聽便宜處決。

translations.literal: for Yi he was specially allowed convenient disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Yi alone was allowed to decide conveniently.

sentences.zh: 久之。

translations.literal: After long time.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval.

sentences.zh: 還翰林，仍領府。

translations.literal: He returned to the Hanlin Academy, still heading the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Hanlin Academy while still heading the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治司農吏盜庫錢獄未竟，中書檢正張諤判寺事，懼失察，以帖詰稽留，繹遣吏示以成牘，言者論其徇宰屬、縱有罪，出知滁州。

translations.literal: The case of Ministry of Revenue clerks stealing treasury funds was not concluded; Zhongshu Inspection Commissioner Zhang E judged temple affairs, fearing oversight failure, used a slip to press delay; Yi sent a clerk to show the completed dossier. Remonstrators argued he favored chief-minister subordinates and indulged guilt—he was sent out to know Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While a revenue theft case remained open, Zhang E pressed delays; Yi showed a finished dossier. Critics said he favored ministerial aides and indulged crime, and he was sent to Chu.

sentences.zh: 郊祀恩，復知制誥，言者再論之，得秘書監、集賢院學士。

translations.literal: By suburban-sacrifice grace he was restored to drafting official; remonstrators debated again and he received Secretariat Director and Academician of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After suburban-sacrifice grace he regained drafting duties; critics objected again and he became secretariat director and Jixian academician.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，知廣州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng he knew Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng he governed Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庫有檀香佛像，繹以木易之。

translations.literal: The treasury had a sandalwood Buddha image; Yi exchanged it for wood.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced a sandalwood Buddha in the treasury with wood.

sentences.zh: 事覺，有司當為官物有剩利。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered the responsible office judged it as surplus profit on government goods.
translations.idiomatic: When discovered, officials judged it surplus profit on government goods.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「是以事佛麗重典矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is using service to Buddha to beautify a heavy statute."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said serving Buddha could not excuse a grave statute.

sentences.zh: 時繹已加龍圖閣待制、知江寧府，乃貶建昌軍，奪其職。

translations.literal: At the time Yi had already been given Academician Awaiting Orders at the Dragon Diagram Hall and knew Jiangning Prefecture; he was then demoted to Jianchang Army and stripped of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Already dragon-diagram academician and Jiangning prefect, he was demoted to Jianchang and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 後復太中大夫以卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: Later restored to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and died at sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Later restored to grand master of palace attendance, he died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 繹為政務摧豪黨，而行與貌違，暮年繆為敦樸之狀，好事者目為「熱熟顏回」。

translations.literal: Yi in governing affairs strove to crush powerful factions, but conduct and appearance diverged; in late years he falsely assumed a look of plain honesty—those who liked affairs called him "Hot Cooked Yan Hui."
translations.idiomatic: Yi crushed powerful factions in office yet his conduct belied his look; in old age he played at plain virtue and wits called him Hot Cooked Yan Hui.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王廣淵在仁宗時，因近昵獻文於英宗潛邸，固已有竊取功名之心，蓋為臣之不忠者，雖列侍從，烏足道哉！

translations.literal: The critique says: Wang Guangyuan in the Renzong era, through near intimacy presented writings to the Yingzong Emperor's hidden residence—he already had a heart stealing fame; as a minister he was disloyal; though listed among attendants, how can he be spoken of!
translations.idiomatic: The historians say Guangyuan curried favor with the future Yingzong as a disloyal seeker of fame unworthy of attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 王陶始為韓琦所知，在御史時，頗能譏切時政，及為中丞，則承望風旨，攻琦如仇讎，欲自取重位，其忘姜愚布衣之義，又不足責矣。

translations.literal: Wang Tao at first was known to Han Qi; as censor he could rather satirize current government, but as censor-in-chief he followed wind and intent, attacked Qi like a deadly foe, wishing to seize a heavy post himself—his forgetting Jiang Yu's kindness in commoner days is again not worth blaming.
translations.idiomatic: Tao began under Han Qi's patronage and criticized policy as censor, but as censor-in-chief he followed court winds, attacked Qi like an enemy for promotion, and forgot Jiang Yu's kindness—hardly surprising.

sentences.zh: 王子韶之陷祖無擇，何正臣之論蘇軾，皆小人之盜名。

translations.literal: Wang Zishao's trapping Zu Wuzi and He Zhengchen's impeaching Su Shi are both petty men's stealing fame.
translations.idiomatic: Zishao's ruin of Zu Wuzi and Zhengchen's attack on Su Shi were petty fame-seeking.

sentences.zh: 陳繹希合用事，固無足道，然於獄事多所平反，惜乎閨門不肅，廉恥並喪，雖明曉吏事，亦何取焉。

translations.literal: Chen Yi curried favor with those in power and is truly not worth speaking of; yet in prison affairs he reversed many cases—pity that his household was not disciplined and integrity and shame were both lost; though clear in official matters, what is there to take?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi flattered the powerful and is barely worth mention, yet he reversed many cases; pity his household was disorderly and shameless—official skill alone could not redeem him.
